description: Hemispherical cup resting on an annular foot; used for drinking.
Plate with oblique marli decorated with broad festooned appendages.
Plate with a foot and a marli rim.
Carinated bowl with a marli-type rim.
Hemispherical bowl with a horizontal, oblique or curved marli; annular foot of varying height.
Deep plate with broad oblique marli often guilloche-decorated; occasionally with a moulded tail handle.
Dish with incurved wall and thickened (var.A) or thin (var.B) rim; productions C1, C2.
Dish with rounded convex body and thin converging rim.
Plate/dish with truncated-conical body and wide floor on a small annular foot.
Plate/dish with truncated-conical body, narrower floor than 50A, with little or no annular foot.
Flaring bowl with convex floor and internal guilloche decoration.
Plate with flaring bowl and a flat marli (rim shelf).
Hemispherical bowl with flaring, thickened and notched (toothed) lip.
Hemispherical bowl with a horizontal, grooved rim.
Hemispherical bowl with flaring rim or marli shelf.
Hemispherical bowl with flaring rim and a beaded (bourrelet) lip.
Carinated bowl with a grooved band rim.
Plate with carinated bowl and a collar (collerette) rim.
Plate with a marli and a collar (collerette) lip.
Plate with truncated-conical bowl, annular foot and a beaded rim.
Dish with rounded bowl, thickened rim and a tall foot.
Dish with straight-sided bowl, tall foot and a band rim.
Hemispherical cup with a flattened-thickened rim, external guilloche decoration and a tall foot.
Ovoid jug with a tall narrow neck and an annular foot.
Ovoid amphora with a tall neck and two handles.
Hemispherical bowl with a flaring rim featuring a grooved gutter.
Conical lid with an internal lug and an upturned rim.
Plate/dish with a rounded basin and a flat marli rim.
Plate with a marli rim, occurring in a small (var. A) and a large (var. B) size.
Low dish/cup with an oblique marli rim.
Low cup with a marli rim decorated with rouletting or stamping.
Plate or cup with an incurved collar-shaped rim.
Plate with an oblique marli rim.
Plate with a marli rim and a flat floor.
Ovoid carinated jug with a short neck and a flaring rim; single handle.
Globular carinated jug with a tall conical neck; single handle.
Open bowl with an external collar rim and a guilloche-decorated floor.
Amphora with globular body, low neck, and a collar-shaped rim; two handles.
Bulbous body with rim meeting the shoulder at a right angle; rounded or bluntly pointed base. Transport/storage amphora.
Slightly bulging cylindrical body, rim at a right angle to the shoulder, rounded convex base.
Body swollen toward the base, thickened convergent rim, rounded shoulder, ogival base.
Similar to the preceding form but taller and narrower.
Body swollen at the base, thickened rim, straight upper belly, ogival base.
Bitruncated-conical profile, straight upper belly, rolled rim continuing the wall without a shoulder, V-shaped base.
Bitruncated-conical profile with concave upper belly, rolled rim continuing the wall without a shoulder, V-shaped base.
Narrow variant with a more elongated lip; elongated spindle body tapering to a point.
Very narrow variant of the previous types; pointed base sometimes moulded.
Wide ovoid body with marked shoulder, cylindrical neck, divergent almond-shaped rim, hollow spool foot.
Globular body, cylindrical neck distinct from shoulder, thickened roughly triangular lip, small pointed base.
Ovoid body, elongated neck, divergent rim with external moulding.
Elongated fusiform body, concave neck, triangular-section rim, pivot base.
Spindle-shaped body with sloping shoulder, cylindrical neck, rounded bead rim, elbowed handles.
Elongated amphora with a tall neck lacking a shoulder; thick band-like rim; flattened, bent handles; ending in a hollow pointed base.
Narrow cylindrical-bodied amphora without a neck; short flaring rim with a moulded lip; small handles set below the shoulder; flattened ogival base.
Amphora with flaring, often moulded rim; ovoid body; short handles of oval or bifid section; hollow pointed foot.
Apulian amphora with rounded roll rim, cylindrical neck, short round-sectioned handles, globular body and a spool/reel-shaped foot.
Brindisi amphora with a bulging body, rolled lip, short massive round-sectioned handles and a small pointed foot.
Beaded rim often showing folding traces, the internal hollow not always visible, systematically underlined by a low marked listel; found on A-MGR 1.
Folded beaded almond-shaped rim, folding hollow sometimes visible, nearly always with a thin listel beneath; found on A-MGR 2 and 3.
Rim with horizontal marli; attested on types A-MGR 4 to A-MGR 6.
Rim with inclined marli; attested on types A-MGR 4 to A-MGR 6.
Cylindrical amphora with a vertical band rim, sometimes set off by an external ridge.
Cylindrical amphora with a convex band rim; care needed not to confuse with form A-AFR 57.
Cylindrical amphora with a thin vertical band rim.
Amphora with low neck often decorated with striations; massive rounded bead rim with a flattened lip.
Large cylindrical amphora with a high neck; thin band rim pinched off; everted flattened lip; short ribbed foot.
Medium cylindrical amphora; low neck with straight flaring rim; tapered lip (var.A-B) sometimes with an external projection (var.C).
Hellenistic Chian-type amphora with biconical body, small ridged rim, very tall cylindrical neck, long round-section handles, and a slightly hollow button foot.
Chian-type variant with a more fusiform body, same neck and rim as Chi5 but ending in a pointed foot.
General series gathering all amphorae of Clazomenae and related products.
Amphora with marked cylindrical neck, oval-section handles, rounded rim, ovoid body and low ring base, often painted with bands on rim and body.
Plain bulbous amphora with cylindrical neck, rounded rim and low ring base.
Amphora with fusiform body, tall cylindrical neck, elongated rounded rim and hollow button base.
Amphora with fusiform body and marked shoulder, truncated-conical neck, elongated rounded rim and button base.
Variant with more swollen body, same rim and neck, curved handles and a truncated-cone or cylindrical base topped by a plastic ring.
General series covering all amphorae of Cnidus and related types.
Probably broad ovoid body; neck flaring upward; thin almond rim with marked listel set low; pronounced groove at neck-body junction.
Milesian amphora with almond rim; more or less flaring neck with marked ridge at base; bent oval-section handles; hollow button foot with constricted base.
General series of amphorae from Peparethos and Ikos.
Conical body; cylindrical neck about a third of total height; marked shoulder; flat or slightly curved beaded rim; foot continuing body line ending in a slightly projecting heel.
Pithoid body; short neck; slightly drooping rim (mushroom or swan-neck type); terminal button strongly hollowed at base.
General series of amphorae from Rhodes or related; broad chronological range.
Long cylindrical neck; triangular rim; oval-section handles; bitruncated body; angular button foot.
Variant of Rho1 with a shorter body; button foot often hollow.
Rhodian-type amphora with cylindrical neck, ribbon-shaped lip, triangular body from a sharply inflected shoulder, and a solid button foot.
Rhodian-type amphora with tall cylindrical neck, small rounded-roll lip, round-sectioned elbow handles, ovoid body and a small pivot base.
Rhodian-type amphora, variant of the preceding with a more elongated body.
Rhodian-type amphora with same neck and rim, sharply angular handles peaked at top, tapering body and narrow pivot base.
Late evolution of the Rhodian tradition, partly Italian production, with a very narrow body extending the neck.
Rhodian-tradition amphora, variant of the preceding form with a body widening toward the bottom.
Series grouping all amphorae of Samos or related production.
Italic Dressel 1 amphora, variant A: height 0.90–1.10 m, fairly low spindle-shaped body, slightly angular or rounded shoulder, short often triangular lip (sometimes short banded, under 5.5 cm).
Triangular rim, more or less elongated, with concave base.
Triangular or short banded rim with horizontal base.
Triangular or short banded rim with oblique base.
Italic Dressel 1 amphora, variant B: larger than 1A (height 110–120 cm), cylindrical neck, sharply angular shoulder, tall massive foot (>15 cm), and a tall banded lip (>5.5 cm).
Banded rim with concave base.
Banded rim with horizontal base.
Banded rim with oblique base.
Iberian amphora with sinuous profile; widest diameter usually in the lower belly; very open pointed base.
Small amphora (half-measure?); cylindrical body with very open pointed base.
Amphora similar to R7 but with a pointed pivot base.
Amphora with nearly horizontal shoulder, cylindrical body and V-shaped base.
Divergent rim with rounded lip.
Parallel-sided rim with rounded lip.
Convergent convex rim with rounded lip.
Convergent concave rim with rounded lip.
Divergent rim with thickened rounded lip.
Parallel-sided rim with thickened rounded lip.
Convergent convex rim with thickened rounded lip.
Thasian amphora with incurved neck, lip in a small rounded bead, triangular body profile and a hollow button or short pivot base.
Thasian amphora with tall incurved neck, small bead rim, biconical body ending in a very long hollowed pivot toe.
Thasian amphora with cylindrical neck, everted lip rim, spindle-shaped (fusiform) body and a short solid pivot toe.
Samian or related amphora with flaring neck on a marked base, small rounded rim, broad ovoid body and narrow diverging ring foot.
Variant of Sam1 with a more slender, elongated body.
Variant with elongated ovoid body.
Samian or related amphora with short cylindrical neck, almond-shaped rim, fairly broad oval body and small ring foot.
Ovoid amphora with unmarked neck-shoulder junction, tall neck often with a ridge, almond rim with convex opening and narrow slightly hollow spool foot.
Samian-attributed amphore, slightly flaring cylindrical neck, triangular rim, oval-section handles, elongated ovoid body and hollow button toe.
General series covering all Thasian and related amphorae; see Garlan and other references.
Thasian or related amphora with overall lozenge profile, converging neck, small triangular lip and pivot toe hollowed at the base.
Thasian or related amphora, second type per Bon's classification.

Spindle-shaped, more or less bulging body with a tapered foot; low wide truncated-cone neck (var.A) or narrow (var.B) or tall neck (var.C); short rounded ribbed-section handles; flanged rim with external projection and internal groove (var.A-B) or plain band (var.C); coarse beige fabric.
Wide neck flaring at top; triangular rim; piriform body; tall hollow foot; yellowish to brown fabric with impurities and white slip.
Like B2b but with a more compact piriform body; porous beige to yellowish fabric with white slip.
Spindle-shaped body with hollow conical foot, neckless; rim of triangular (var.A), rounded (var.B) or thin (var.C) section; massive handles applied on the rim; coarse beige fabric.
Often moulded everted rim; ovoid body; short handles of oval or bifid section; tall hollow foot; yellowish, sometimes pink or greenish-beige fabric. Used for garum and salted fish.
Spindle-shaped amphora, more bulging than other Dr.7/11 forms, with a collar-type rim; fine beige to pinkish fabric. For garum or salted fish.
Same general shape as Dr.9 but with a flanged band rim; beige to pinkish fabric. For salted fish and more rarely wine.
Cylindrical amphora with a short, often hollow foot and a low neck ending in a flared band rim.
Cylindrical amphora with a hollow base; low neck with a convex band rim and an internal groove.
Cylindrical amphora with an almond-shaped or rounded band rim, sometimes underlined by a slight external step (with or without step variants).
Lesbian amphora with spherical body, short cylindrical neck topped by a thick rounded rim without listel; neck-body junction marked by a groove; narrow flat base.
Lesbian amphora with wide ovoid body, cylindrical neck topped by a thick rounded rim without listel; neck-body junction marked by a groove; fairly wide flat base.
Lesbian amphora with cylindrical neck, almond-shaped rim with mouldings, massive round-section handles, ovoid body ending in a fairly broad flat base.
Lesbian amphora with tall cylindrical neck, everted rim emphasized by a moulding, round-section handles, ovoid body ending in a fine pivot toe.
Lesbian amphora with tall cylindrical neck, everted rim emphasized by a moulding, round-section handles, ovoid body ending in a flat pivot toe.
Lesbian amphora with long cylindrical neck, small beaded rim, round-section handles, elongated triangular body ending in a pivot toe.
Series grouping all amphorae of Mende and related types.
Mende amphora with cylindrical neck, beaded rim emphasized by mouldings, well-marked shoulder and a flaring pivot toe.
Series grouping all amphorae of Miletus and related types.
General series header for Attic transport amphorae; covers all Attic transport amphora types.

Attic 'SOS' amphora, 'Middle' variant; spindle-shaped ovoid body, cylindrical neck with marked neck-body join, almond rim often with a fillet, oval-section handles, fairly tall ring foot; painted decoration in black or red-brown with shoulder bands and concentric circles and zigzag on the neck.
Attic 'SOS' amphora, 'Late I' variant; more rounded, fuller belly than the Middle variant.
Attic 'SOS' amphora, 'Late II' variant; evolution of preceding types with a less marked, concave neck and a tall convex lip.

Brush-painted Attic amphora; ovoid body, almond-shaped rim, oval-section handles, unmarked neck-body junction, ring foot with diverging walls; rim and body covered with brown-to-black paint applied with a brush in horizontal strokes on the wheel.
Horizontal amphora rim, found notably on types 1 and LWa/b.
Inclined rim with horizontal base, attested on types LWc and d.
Inclined rim with oblique base, attested on types LWc, d, e.
Inclined rim with concave base, attested on types LWc, d, e.
Elongated rim, attested notably on type LWe.
Squat, bulbous Greco-Italic amphora, 60-70 cm tall, max belly diameter 38-40 cm, with an elongated sometimes hollow foot and generally Bd1-type rims; made in Sicily and probably Magna Graecia.
Taller (70-80 cm) and less bulbous (max diameter 36-38 cm) than LWa, with a short sometimes hollow foot and generally Bd1-type rim; produced in Sicily and probably Magna Graecia.
Slender amphora 82-90 cm tall, max belly diameter 36-39 cm, fitted with Bd2, 3 or 4 rims; also occurs as a half-amphora 55-60 cm tall; Italian origin.
"Standard" Greco-Italic spindle-shaped amphora, 75-85 cm tall, max belly diameter 32-36 cm, with an elongated solid foot and Bd2, 3 or 4 rim; probably from central and southern Italy.
Greco-Italic amphora variant equated with the Laubenheim type (description truncated on page).
Gauloise 1 amphora with ring base and pot-bellied profile (max diameter at mid-height). Very short neck; rim quarter-round or triangular with horizontal upper part; flat moulded handles.
Gauloise 2 amphora with ring base and ovoid profile. Cylindrical neck; moulded rim; flat moulded handles.
Gauloise 3 amphora with ring base and ovoid body (max diameter in upper part); neck taller than A-GAUL 1; rim with external double inflexion and rounded edge; bifid oval-section handles.
Gauloise 4 amphora with narrow ring base; ovoid body; rounded (rolled) rim; handles with central groove.
Variant of Gauloise 4 with short neck and thin almond-shaped rim.
Gauloise 5 amphora with ring base and bulbous body (max diameter in upper or middle of belly); slightly flaring neck; thickened horizontal rim.
Gauloise 6 amphora with flat base; narrow neck; thickened rim with internal protrusion.
Cylindrical amphora with strongly flaring neck, divergent moulded rim and a hollow-pointed toe.
Narrow cylindrical body, concave flaring neck, divergent rim with thickened drooping lip; handles below shoulder; long solid pointed toe.
Narrow cylindrical body with short neck and strongly flaring lip; handles below shoulder; solid pointed toe.
Broad cylindrical body, thick vertical rim continuing the wall line, hollow base; 'Numance camp' amphora.
Carinated bulging shoulder, body strongly narrowed below the carination, max diameter low; small vertical lip barely set off from body.
Shell-shaped (obus) profile widening downward, carinated shoulder, convergent rim with flattened thickened lip, V-shaped base.
Variant of Ch3, narrower and more angular in profile.
Punic amphora with carinated shoulder and ovoid body; ribbon handles on the shoulder (description continues on next page).
Spindle-shaped amphora with an everted band rim.
Spindle-shaped amphora with short body and hollow tip, rim formed as a thick bead.
Ovoid amphora with pointed base and a flaring band rim.
Ovoid amphora with tall neck and a band rim with flattened lip.

Corinthian-type transport amphora; marked cylindrical neck with rounded or elongated rolled rim often emphasized by a relief listel; oval-section handles; globular body tapering to a spinning-top base; flat bottom. Rim type A-MGR Bd1.
Cylindrical neck with elongated rolled rim underlined by a moulding; oval-section handles; ovoid body; button base often slightly hollowed underneath. Rim type A-MGR Bd2.
Magna Graecia amphora, late variant of the archaic type; almond-section rim; tall bulging neck; spindle-shaped body; solid button foot. Rim type Bd2.
Magna Graecia or Sicilian type; globular carinated body with wide neck; small solid or hollow foot. Rim type A-MGR Bd3 or 4.
Magna Graecia or Sicilian type, sometimes called 'proto-Greco-Italic'; globular carinated body with rather narrow flaring neck; small hollow foot. Rim type A-MGR Bd3 or 4.
Magna Graecia or Sicilian type; spindle-shaped body with flaring neck; elongated solid foot. Rim type A-MGR Bd3 or 4.
Possible Locrian amphora; cylindrical neck with everted triangular lip; ovoid body; thin walls; hollow button base.
Large cylindrical amphora with tall neck and triangular band rim; short ringed foot.
Large cylindrical amphora with tall neck and band rim accented by a pinch at the neck; short ringed foot.
Large cylindrical amphora with tall neck having a median flexure and a triangular rim; short ringed foot.
Large cylindrical amphora with tall neck having a median flexure and a curved collar rim; short ringed foot, similar to A-AFR Tr3b.
Amphora with a truncated-cone neck bearing a striated band and an oval bead rim.
Amphora close to A-GAUL 4 with handled neck.
Ovoid amphora with pointed base and band rim (early Tripolitanian type).
Cylindrical amphora with vertical neck and massive band rim (Tripolitanian I).
Dressel 1C variant: spindle-shaped body, rounded or S-profile handles, flaring neck, tall band or closed-triangular rim (often over 6 cm high).
Close to Dressel 1C and A-GR-ITA LWe: tall vessel (95-100 cm), max body diameter ~30 cm, short rim about 3 cm high.
Lamboglia 2 amphora: triangular or short band rim, wide neck, weak shoulder, max diameter low on the body, solid pointed toe.
Bullet-shaped (obus) body without neck, vertical flattened rim, grooved shoulder and lower body, small stubby handles, slightly flattened base. Wine, sometimes oil.
Globular grooved body, convex base, tall cylindrical neck, rolled (bourrelet) rim, small oval-section handles; powdery sandy beige to orange fabric. Wine.
Globular grooved body, convex base, short band-like neck, small oval-section handles; well-fired sandy fabric, red core and grey surface. Wine.
Spindle-shaped grooved body, tapering pointed base, cylindrical neck with rounded lip, small oval-section handles; laminated chocolate-brown micaceous fabric. Wine.
Spindle-shaped amphora close to Dr.2/4 but distinguished by its tall neck, oval-section handles and ringed foot. Wine.
Ovoid body with cylindrical neck, elbowed handles of bifid or grooved oval section, small pointed foot. Wine.
Carinated ovoid body without neck, rolled (bourrelet) rim, pointed base, long handles topped with a small appendage. Wine.
Fusiform amphora with high foot, tall narrow neck and a band-shaped rim; well-fired beige to pinkish fabric, used for garum and fish sauces.
Cylindrical-bodied amphora with high conical foot and tall neck ending in a thin or beaded rim; granular beige to pink fabric with beige slip, for fish sauces.
Small amphora with spindle-shaped body, high foot and a collar-shaped rim; probably for fish sauces.
Generic series grouping any indeterminate variant of the Dressel 20 amphora.
Ovoid body with pointed base, almond-shaped lip and massive round-section handles; beige, greyish or pink very sandy fabric, used for olive oil.
Globular body with pointed base, almond rim with internal hollow and massive round-section handles; very sandy beige to pink fabric, for olive oil.
Variant of the preceding with a thicker, more triangular rim; globular oil amphora in very sandy beige to pink fabric.
Amphora with sinuous body whose maximum diameter is in the lower part; thickened diverging or parallel rim; weakly marked shoulder.
Amphora with maximum diameter in the lower body, no neck, convergent rim, angular shoulder and an ogival (pointed-rounded) base.
Amphora with truncated-conical profile; everted rim, no neck; rounded bullet-shaped (obus) base.
Cylindrical amphora with short neck, diverging rim with moulded lip and a pointed base.
Cylindrical-bodied amphora with short neck, band rim, two handles below the shoulder and a button base.
Narrow cylindrical amphora with short neck and flaring moulded lip, two handles below the shoulder, and an ogival base.
Convex bulging rim formed by folding the neck wall outward; a hollow remains in the bourrelet thickness, with the exterior bead set off by a more or less marked rounded listel.

More elongated, less bulging rim than type 1, sometimes with a slight oblique flattening at top; the folding hollow is reduced and elongated, with a relief listel usually marking the base of the bead.
Elongated rim with rounded profile, similar to some type-2 rims but solid, without the folding hollow; elongated bead set off by a moulding beneath the lip.
Intermediate form between bd3 and bd5; fairly elongated rounded rim, upper flat inclined outward making a softened angle with the bulging part, base usually marked by mouldings.
Thick, stocky faceted rim with a small oblique often concave flat at top, then two more or less marked facets sometimes softened; one or two deep grooves set off a listel beneath the lip.

Quarter-circle profile rim with upper flat inclined outward; thickened lip underlined by a rounded or angular listel set off by deep grooves; the upper flat is concave forming an angular edge externally.
Rim with horizontal upper marli and quarter-circle profile, set off at its lower part by mouldings.
Quarter-circle rim with upper marli inclined outward, lacking mouldings at the base of the lip, which connects directly to the neck.
Tall flaring neck with an inturned rim accented by an exterior groove; narrow spindle-shaped body tapering to a solid pointed toe.
Amphora with bifid elbowed handles, long cylindrical neck, sloping shoulder, thick rounded everted lip and a small solid pointed foot.
Amphora with very flaring lip, narrow more or less tall truncated-conical neck, oval-section handles and an elongated hollow pointed base.
Globular body with pointed base; triangular rim often grooved inside with a rounded lip; massive round-sectioned handles. Sandy beige to greyish/rosé fabric.
Globular body, pointed base; triangular rim sharper than var. D with flattened lip and very deep internal groove; massive round-sectioned handles.
Globular body with pointed base; triangular rim without internal groove; massive round-sectioned handles. Sandy beige to greyish/rosé fabric.
Globular body, pointed base; thick triangular rim tending to become rounded; massive round-sectioned handles.
Ovoid body with pointed base; triangular rim with slight internal gorge; round-sectioned handles often applied on the rim. Sandy beige/grey/rosé fabric.
Ovoid body with pointed base; band rim with internal gorge; round-sectioned handles often applied on the rim. Sandy beige/grey/rosé fabric.
Ovoid body with pointed base; flaring rim; round-sectioned handles. Sandy beige/grey/rosé fabric.
Narrow cylindrical body with carinated shoulder, tall neck with beaded rim and long elbowed handles.
Bulging ribbed body, convex base, round-section handles with external ribs, wide cylindrical neck with beaded or collared rim; greyish to rosé fabric with white grit.
Bulging ribbed body, convex base, round-section ribbed handles, narrow cylindrical neck with beaded or collared rim; greyish to rosé fabric with white grit and frequent red painted inscriptions.
Spherical body with finely striated shoulder, short oval-section handles, flaring band rim; fine micaceous brown or light orange fabric.
Globular body with finely striated shoulder, short oval-section handles, truncated-conical neck with vertical band rim; fine micaceous brown or light orange fabric.
Small amphora with ribbed body, carinated or rounded shoulder, navel foot, narrow neck with small handles; fine very micaceous brown/red fabric.
Small spindle-shaped amphora with oblique flutings, button foot, narrow neck with small handles; fine very micaceous brown/red fabric.
Amphora with rounded body and small loop handles set high near the rim; bag-shaped Late Roman 4 type.
Cnidian-type transport amphora with a long nearly cylindrical neck, vertical handles and a ringed foot.
Cnidian-type amphora with body widening downward, tall cylindrical neck, small beaded lip, elbowed bifid handles and a ringed foot.
General series grouping all Corinthian or related amphorae.
Corinthian amphora (type A ancien) with cylindrical neck, overhanging horizontal flat rim, massive round-section handles, globular body and a flat base edged with a ridge.
Corinthian amphora (type A récent / A') with spindle-shaped body, triangular rim, round-section handles and a button base.
Corinthian amphora (type A récent), variant with low globular squat body.
Corinthian amphora (type A récent) with spherical body, tall straight neck, band rim and a cone-shaped foot.

"Corinthian" amphora (type B ancien, also made at Corcyra) with marked cylindrical neck, rounded or elongated beaded rim often with a relief listel, oval-section handles, globular spinning-top body and flat base.
Bulging-bodied amphora with short lip and thin walls; angular handles flattened in section at the base; narrow flat base with unthickened wall. Two paste variants (grey-yellow or pinkish-orange).

Broad ovoid body with short lip on a small distinct neck; rounded handles with round section at base; bullet-shaped (often domed) base, rarely pointed. Many brown/red/orange paste variants with frequent cream slip, volcanic temper.
Narrow spindle-shaped (fusiform) body; short lip on a well-defined small neck; oval-profile handles, round at base; pointed or bullet base, rarely domed. Same paste and slip variants as 3A.
Bulging-bodied amphora with a large elongated rolled rim; massive round-section handles; pointed or slightly flattened base; brown-red to red paste with thick white slip.

Bulging-bodied form; lip welded to the body with oval elongated section, no distinct neck; massive round-section handles; pinched/flattened-pointed base; brown paste with grey-black core, cream slip, volcanic temper.

Ovoid to more fusiform profile; round-section handles; bullet-shaped domed base sometimes with start of a point in later examples; distinctive very elongated, straight, flaring and barely thickened rim.

"Bon-Porté" type: more or less elongated bulging body; thick rolled lip, sometimes hanging outward or elongated; round or oval handles that may rise above the mouth; flat base of variable diameter, rarely concave; usually yellow or orange paste.
Large cylindrical amphora, close to type A-AFR 35a in shape.
Large cylindrical amphora with low neck and rim having a flat outer face underlined by a step; Keay 33 may be a variant.
Large cylindrical amphora with high neck; collar rim with flat outer face; incised wavy line on the neck.
Large cylindrical amphora with high neck and rounded collar rim.
Large cylindrical amphora with high neck; collar rim with flattened lip.
Large cylindrical amphora with low neck; thin rim with external step (var.A) or almond-shaped rim (var.B).
Massaliote amphora variant defined by rim types 1, 2 and 3; earliest form of the series.
Massaliote amphora with rim types 2, 3, 3/5 and 4.
Massaliote amphora with rim types 4, 5 and 6.
Massaliote amphora with rim types 5 through 9.
Massaliote amphora with rim types 7 through 10.
Latest massaliote amphora with rim types 10 or 11.
Carinated shoulder with small divergent rim angled off the shoulder; sinuous body widening toward the base; pointed (shell-shaped) bottom.
Carinated shoulder with a small incurved divergent rim; globular body widening downward; rounded or very obtuse-angled base.
Gently carinated rounded shoulder with a small everted rim; globular body widening downward; rounded base.
Sinuous profile with greatest diameter low on the body; outturned rim; rounded shoulder; bulging base.
Similar to R1 but with an ovoid profile.
Elongated sinuous body; convergent rim with thickened lip; rounded shoulder; ogival base with rounded bottom.
Continuous rounded profile; rounded, more or less incurving shoulder; fairly open ogival base.
Narrow fusiform profile; convergent rim with thickened lip; rounded shoulder; cylindrical body; pointed ogival base.
Same shape as R5 but with a more elongated body.
Ovoid-bodied amphora with elbowed handles and a beaded (rounded) rim; used for wine and brine.
Spindle-shaped (fusiform) amphora with flaring neck and band-shaped rim; used for brine.
Amphora with ovoid body, flaring neck and thickened rim; produced at Fréjus, used for brine.
Spindle-shaped amphora with flaring neck and beaded rim, from Fréjus; for fish and sauces.
Flat-bottomed ovoid amphora with a flaring triangular rim, Fréjus-Lenzburg type; possibly for brine.
Spindle-shaped amphora with flaring neck.
Band or triangular rim with concave base.
Band or triangular rim with horizontal base.
Band or triangular rim with oblique base.
Long band rim.
Short band or triangular rim with concave base.
Short band or triangular rim with horizontal base.
Amphora derived from an East Greek type; spinning-top (toupie) shaped body, tall cylindrical neck, rim made of a folded round bead.
Half-module amphora with toupie or spherical body, short flaring neck and a bevelled rounded-bead rim.
Amphora with toupie or spherical body, short flaring neck and a rim usually with facets.
Amphora with ovoid body, short neck and a rim most often shaped as a quarter circle.
Amphora with ovoid body, tall cylindrical neck and a rim usually in quarter-circle profile.
Half-module amphora with ovoid body, tall cylindrical neck and a rim usually in quarter-circle profile.
Amphora with ovoid, fusiform body, tall cylindrical neck, rim of varied section with soft profile and a marli usually tilted inward; hollow spool-shaped foot.
Imitation of the Greco-Italic amphore; triangular bd10/bd11 rim, tall cylindrical neck, ovoid body and solid pointed foot.
Spindle-shaped amphora with a carinated shoulder, cylindrical neck, rounded thickened rim, and bent (elbowed) handles. Used for wine.
Spindle-shaped amphora tapering downward, with a narrow neck and thickened rim; brick-colored fabric sometimes with pinkish surface. Used for oil.
Spindle-shaped amphora without neck, with a rounded beaded rim and small oval-section handles. Used for fruit.
Amphora with fusiform body and hollow toe; flaring neck with rounded rim; handles set on the shoulder. Yellowish to brown fabric with inclusions, white slip.
Variant of B4A with identical fabric; thinner triangular rim with an internal groove.
Spindle-shaped amphora with short body and hollow toe; thick beaded rim. Granular beige to pinkish fabric with many inclusions, beige to greenish slip.

Spindle body without neck; hollow conical foot; rim either projecting beaded (var.A), rounded beaded (var.B) or thin (var.C); oval-section handles applied at the rim. Fine dark brown to orange-pink fabric. Used for fish sauces.
Amphora with rounded truncated-cone body, narrow flat base with ring foot, short neck and half-rounded rim; flattened handles with a more or less marked central rib. Used for transport and storage.
Known only from fragments; cylindrical or flaring neck, flattened projecting half-torus rim, ribbed handles.
Imitation of Dressel 1B; tall cylindrical neck, elongated vertical band rim, straight oval-section handles, carinated shoulder.
Imitation of Dressel 2-4; spindle-shaped body, cylindrical neck, rounded bead rim, elbowed pseudo-bifid handles.
Imitation of Dressel 7-11; spindle-shaped body, wide flaring neck, moulded rim with double step or short band, pseudo-bifid handle, hollow pointed base.
Imitation of Léétanienne 1; cylindrical neck, convex band rim, pseudo-bifid handle.
Imitation of Pascual 1; spindle-shaped body, tall narrow flaring neck, long band rim, pseudo-bifid or ribbed handles.
Imitation of a piriform amphora; neck continuing the body, wide and narrowing upward, band rim, pseudo-bifid or ribbed handles.
Attic 'brush-painted' amphora; squatter variant with cylindrical neck, short rolled rim and a lower ring foot.
Series grouping all Chalcidian and related transport amphorae.
Chalcidian brush-painted amphora; elongated molded rim, unmarked neck, globular body and low ring base.
Series grouping all Chian and related transport amphorae.
Chian spindle-shaped amphora; small rolled rim, wide neck over concave shoulder, narrow ring foot; red bands on white/yellowish slip with horizontal lines and a reclining S on the shoulder.
Chian amphora variant with a more distinct cylindrical neck, oval-section handles, ovoid body and small narrow hollow foot.
Chian amphora variant with thicker rolled rim and slightly flaring neck.
Chian amphora variant with a slimmer, slightly bulging neck, simplified or absent painted decor and a thin round-sectioned rim.
Chian amphora with elongated ovoid body, tall narrow hollow foot, no decoration, bulging neck sometimes grooved at junction with body and a small rolled rim.
Cylindrical grooved body with short ringed foot, short neck, beaded rim with or without internal groove, short oval-section handles applied on the rim; beige fabric with quartz temper.

Spindle-shaped, more or less rounded body with tapered foot; low truncated-conical or tall neck; short rounded oval-section handles often grooved; rim as a band with external projection and internal groove or a plain band; coarse beige fabric.
Ovoid body with short foot and short neck; beaded rim with internal groove; oval-section handles applied on the rim; fine beige to bright orange fabric.
Gauloise 7: bulging body with maximum diameter at mid-height, horizontal or rounded (boudin) rim, truncated-conical neck with a relief listel, and a low ring base.
Gauloise 8: low ring base, unknown body profile, a relief ring on the neck at the upper handle attachment, and a thickened rim with an external groove.
Gauloise 9: bulging body (max diameter mid-height), inclined band rim, flat double-grooved handles, and a low wide ring base.
Spindle-shaped amphore with narrow neck and almond-shaped rim; production of Le Castellet (Var).
Spindle-shaped amphore with elbowed (angled) handles; production of Mandelieu (Var).
Globular flat-bottomed amphore with quadrangular rim; production of Normandy.
Spindle-shaped amphore with a band rim.
Amphora with globular body, hollow underside and ring foot; short neck with pulley-shaped rim. Hard sandy fabric, pale yellow surface, grey core. Probably wine.
Amphora with tall narrow neck, flaring band rim, bifid handles, elongated ovoid body and tall foot. Fine grey-pink fabric close to Dr20. Wine.
Amphora with spindle-shaped body, tall cylindrical or troncoconic neck, incurved collar rim and tall hollow foot. Fine light beige to yellowish fabric. Fish sauces (saumures).
Transport amphora with cylindrical body and neck; rounded bead rim or with oblique flattened lip; bifid elbowed handles; short foot. A variant of the Cos type.
Ovoid body with carinated shoulder; truncated-conical neck with collar rim; oval-section handles; tapered/pointed foot. Probably Istro-Pontic region.
Cretan amphora with ovoid body ending in a short rounded foot; cylindrical neck with bead rim; elbowed round-section handles.
Egyptian spindle-shaped amphora with tall cylindrical neck; short oval-section handles; thin rounded or inward-marli rim.
Kapitän type I amphora; narrow or bulbous spindle body with pointed base; cylindrical neck with elbowed round-section handles; thin rim. Probably eastern Aegean.
Kapitän type II amphora; spindle body on a narrow ring foot; ribbed truncated-conical neck with band rim; high elbowed oval-section grooved handles. Aegean.
Quarter-circle profile rim with a horizontal upper marli attaching directly to the neck, without mouldings; marli straight or slightly concave, soft with rounded angles.

Quarter-circle rim evolving toward soft rounded forms; marli tilted inward, with flat, hollow or convex upper face; usually joined directly to neck, sometimes a groove sets off a slightly pendent lip bead.
Triangular-section rim elongated outward, imitating early Greco-Italic amphorae.
Triangular-section rim with a concave base, imitating later Greco-Italic amphorae.
Convergent concave rim with a rounded, thickened lip; used for transport and storage.
Divergent rim with a flattened lip; used for transport and storage.
Parallel-walled rim with a flattened lip; used for transport and storage.
Convergent convex rim with a flattened lip; used for transport and storage.
Convergent concave rim with a flattened lip; used for transport and storage.
Divergent rim with a flattened, thickened lip; used for transport and storage.
Parallel-walled rim with a flattened, thickened lip; used for transport and storage.
Convergent convex rim with a flattened, thickened lip; used for transport and storage.
Convergent concave rim with a flattened, thickened lip; used for transport and storage.
Cylindrical amphora with a collar (collerette) rim and low-set handles.
Cylindrical amphora with a grooved (cannelée) shoulder and an everted rim forming a concave band.
Late variant of Tr3 with a tall neck and a banded rim showing a double external step.
Globular carinated amphora on an annular foot, with a narrow neck and a convex banded rim hollowed internally.
Amphora with rounded truncated-conical body, narrow flat bottom on a ring foot, short flaring neck, projecting band rim, and flattened grooved handles.
Amphora with rounded truncated-conical body, narrow flat bottom and ring foot, short flaring neck, inward-leaning band rim, and flattened grooved handles.
Amphora with rounded truncated-conical body, narrow flat bottom on a ring foot, short neck, double-stepped rim, and flattened handles with or without a groove.
Amphora variant with a biconical body profile; thickened, turned-out lip.
Amphora variant with a more cylindrical body profile; thickened everted lip.
Amphora with elongated body, cylindrical upper part widening downward, conical lower part, high carinated shoulder, and thickened turned-out lip.
Amphora variant with a higher, more vertical rim than the preceding form.
Amphora with bulging lower belly (max diameter low), cylindrical upper belly, slightly divergent rim continuing the body without a neck, and an obtuse ogival base.
Narrow cylindrical neckless amphora; inturned lip often striated at top, sharply angular shoulder, button base.
Narrow cylindrical neckless amphora with inturned lip, softened angular shoulder, and a rounded base with a very small solid button.
Amphora of unknown (western?) origin; oval rounded rim, short cylindrical neck with a bulging molding, broad ovoid body, narrow low ring foot.
Amphora of unknown (western?) origin; variant of Ind1 with almond-shaped lip and incurved neck, low ring foot.
Amphora of unknown origin; spherical body, short cylindrical neck topped by a barely marked rim, ring foot.
Series grouping all Laconian or related amphorae.
Black-glaze Laconian amphora; ovoid body, cylindrical neck with marked neck-body junction, almond rim sometimes with a listel, ring foot, black glaze over entire exterior.
Laconian amphora; ovoid body, cylindrical neck with marked junction, variable rim (almond or pendant) often with listel, ring foot, black glaze on body and handles, reserved neck.
Laconian amphora; spherical body, marked neck-body junction, fairly short neck, narrow low ring foot, beaded rim underlined by a listel, black glaze or brushed decoration on lower body.
Laconian amphora; ovoid body, morphology like Lac2a but with triangular-profile rim underlined by a listel.
Series grouping all amphorae from Lesbos or related types.
Ovoid amphora on a small foot; short flaring neck; pulley-profile (poulie) rim; granular beige-white fabric. Used for oil.
Amphora with ovoid body and dimpled (umbilicate) base; tall neck; beaded/rolled rim; wide elbowed handles. Used for wine.
Amphora with ovoid body, umbilicate base, tall cylindrical neck, thin everted rim sometimes with pulley profile, high oval-section handles; variable fabric. Used for wine.
Spindle-shaped grooved amphora with weak shoulder; neck continuing the body; almond-shaped rim; flattened ribbed handles. Used for wine or oil.
Globular Baetican olive-oil transport amphora, one of the two main oil forms identified with the province.
Baetican olive-oil amphora, the later companion to Dressel 20 among the main oil forms.
Spindle-shaped fish-sauce amphorae with pointed base and tall flaring neck, grouped as Dressel 7/11; develop mainly in the Augustan period and into the early 2nd c.
Fusiform salting/garum amphora close in form and fabric to the Dressel 7/11 group.
Fusiform salting/garum amphora related to Beltrán 2A and the Dressel 7/11 series.
Later fish-product amphora that becomes predominant as production standardizes, well attested from the 3rd to 5th c.
Late fish-product amphora dominant alongside Beltrán 72 in the 3rd to 5th c.
Ovoid wine amphora with pointed base and tall neck with everted collar rim; widely diffused under Augustus and into the first half of the 1st c.
Medium cylindrical amphora with tall neck, collar-type rim and outward-projecting lip.
Medium cylindrical amphora with tall neck and rounded concave rim, lip tapering/projecting (var. J-O), sometimes heavier or forming a horizontal listel (var. S).
Medium cylindrical amphora with varied rims (beaded or collar), poorly defined variants.
cross_refs: Keay 1984 var. X et suiv., type 28

description: 'Spatheion' with cylindrical shouldered body and narrow neck with collar or rounded beaded rim.
Amphora form (spatheion type) shown by small profile and handle detail.
Medium cylindrical amphora with cylindrical or slightly flaring neck and thickened rim with internal step.
Medium cylindrical amphora with flaring neck and thin rim with rounded, sometimes tapered lip.
Large cylindrical amphora with a cylindrical neck bearing an internal ridge, frequently comb-decorated.
Large cylindrical amphora with a truncated-conical neck showing a striated band and a thin banded rim.
Large cylindrical amphora with a tall neck, almond-shaped rim sometimes with a groove or internal flat, and short ringed foot.
Large cylindrical amphora with cylindrical neck and a marli (flat-flange) rim.
Large cylindrical amphora with tall neck, triangular rim, and short ringed foot.
Large cylindrical amphora with tall neck, banded rim underlined by an external gutter, and short ringed foot.
Narrow cylindrical body without neck; inturned lip; rounded shoulder; convex base ending in a very small solid button.
Amphora with a triangular-section lip, angular shoulder and a very obtuse pointed base.
Amphora with a vertical rim and rounded lip, angular shoulder and a convex base with a small umbilicus; sometimes slipped on the exterior.
Small amphora with fluted piriform body, narrow neck ending in a band rim, and flat base; probably wine.
Amphora with broad cylindro-ovoid body, narrow neck with band rim, ample oval-section handles, and a small pointed foot; wine.
Spindle-shaped amphora recalling Dr2/4 but with a very wide neck, bead rim, and bifid handles with appendage.
Amphora with fluted cylindrical body and neck, high foot, carinated shoulder, and bead rim.
Globular amphora with cylindrical neck, bead rim sometimes with internal groove, and oval-section handles set away from the neck with internal hollow.
Fluted amphora with apparently spindle-shaped body, tall cylindrical neck with projecting faceted rim, and oval-section handles detached from the neck; orange granular fabric.
Ovoid-bodied amphora with narrow ring foot, narrow neck with flared rim, and a single fluted handle.
Corinthian-type amphora with spherical body, straight neck, triangular rim profile underlined by three listels, and a button base.
Corinthian amphora with cylindrical neck, quarter-circle rim leaning outward, oval-section handles, fusiform body and pointed button base.
Corinthian-type amphora with fusiform body broad at the shoulder, cylindrical neck topped by a small triangular rim, handles applied directly to the rim, and a conical base continuing the body line.
Corinthian-type amphora with slender fusiform body narrower than CorB4, straight cylindrical neck slightly inturned with a barely marked rounded rim, and a conical base continuing the body.
General series grouping all amphorae of Cos and related productions.
Cos or related amphora with cylindrical neck, small rounded-bead rim, bifid elbow handles, bitruncated body and a small beveled button base.
Cos or related amphora with cylindrical neck set off from the shoulder by an angle, bifid elbow handles, oblique shoulder, ovoid lower body and a short pointed base.
Cos or related amphora (?) with conical neck, bead rim, angular shoulder, ovoid lower body and a short pointed base.

Amphore vinaire à corps allongé fuselé, lèvre haute presque verticale (col droit), anses verticales en bandeau, fond se terminant par une pointe pleine. Filiation directe avec les amphores gréco-italiques. Variantes illustrées issues de plusieurs épaves (Bon-Porté 2, Pointe Moussure, Pointe Pommègues, Îlot Barthélémy), datées vers 120-80 av. J.-C.

Amphore vinaire à corps allongé presque cylindrique se terminant par une longue pointe massive. Col haut et droit surmonté d'une lèvre haute, verticale et bien différenciée (lèvre épaisse), variant en forme selon les exemplaires. Anses verticales attachées au col et à l'épaule. La planche du bas illustre plusieurs variantes d'épaves (Pointe de Carqueiranne v.50 av. J.-C., Madrague de Giens 75-60 av. J.-C., Plane 1 v.50 av. J.-C., Dramont A milieu Ier s. av. J.-C.) soulignant la diversité des lèvres.

Wine amphora with tall narrow body and an elongated, slender form. Tall cylindrical neck with collar-like rim, vertical handles, and a long solid spike toe; characterized by a more slender, attenuated profile than 1A/1B.

source.item_label: Epave de la Baie de Cavalière, Le Lavandou

description: Amphore vinaire à corps ovoïde s'effilant vers une pointe pleine, col assez haut surmonté d'une lèvre épaissie, deux anses verticales en boudin reliant col et épaule. Variantes datées illustrées : épave de l'Ilot Barthélémy (fin IIe-début Ier s. av. J.-C.), épave de la baie de Cavalière (vers 100 av. J.-C.) et épave Filicudi H (1ère moitié du Ier s. av. J.-C.).

Amphore vinaire à corps ovoïde allongé, col haut développé avec lèvre épaissie, anses verticales s'élevant au-dessus de l'embouchure, et long pied plein effilé en pointe. Difficile à distinguer parfois de la forme Lamboglia 2. Une variante Dressel 6B (Istrie, région d'Aquilée et Trieste) transporte vraisemblablement de l'huile et est diffusée en Italie du Nord et Europe centrale. Variantes illustrées: forme intermédiaire Lamboglia 2 - Dressel 6 (golfe de Fos), épave Aragnon 1 (Sausset-les-Pins), épave de la Tradelière (Cannes, 1er s. av. J.-C.), Dressel 6B (Vérone).

Forme distincte produite en Istrie (région d'Aquilée et Trieste), diffusée surtout en Italie du Nord et en Europe centrale ; corps ovoïde à lèvre épaissie et anses verticales. Exemplaire de Vérone illustré en bas à droite.

Amphore fusiforme/allongée à corps élancé, épaule peu marquée, col court à lèvre épaissie, deux anses verticales courtes, et longue pointe terminale effilée. Variantes illustrées : exemplaire isolé du golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres) et exemplaire de Pompéi antérieur à 79 ap. J.-C.

Amphore vinaire à corps allongé et fuselé se terminant par une pointe pleine; col cylindrique étroit surmonté de deux anses bifides (à double baguette) caractéristiques se relevant verticalement; lèvre simple. La rangée inférieure montre des variantes datées du profil au fil du temps.

Vin amphora with tall cylindrical-ovoid body tapering to a long solid spike toe; tall neck with high arched bifid (double-rod) handles rising above the rim. Bottom row shows several dated profile variants of the type.

Amphore au corps allongé fuselé se terminant par une pointe pleine (toe), col court à lèvre triangulaire et deux anses verticales. La fiche illustre plusieurs exemplaires provenant d'épaves datées : Secca di Capistello (Lipari), Grand-Congloué 1 (Marseille), Chrétienne C (Saint-Raphaël), baie de Briande (Cavalaire), Lazareto (Minorque), mont Rose (Marseille), Punta Scaletta (Île de Giannutri), montrant l'évolution de la forme.

source.figure_label: Epave de la Secca di Capistello (Lipari)

description: Amphore fusiforme à corps allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe basse pleine; col cylindrique étroit surmonté d'une lèvre marquée, deux anses verticales reliant le col à l'épaule. Variantes provinciales illustrées en bas: Nécropole de Pollensa (Majorque) et Golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres).

Flat-bottomed amphora with ovoid body tapering to a low ring/flat base, short neck, everted rim and two arched handles. No spiked toe. The most common Narbonese Gaul wine amphora; variants illustrated from Golfe de Fos, a 3rd c. AD example made at Sallèles d'Aude, and an early 2nd c. AD example from Saint-Raphaël.

Amphore au corps ovoïde à piriforme, col court avec lèvre marquée et deux anses verticales fixées sur l'épaule; base étroite à pied annulaire/petit fond. Variantes illustrées: épave des Roches d'Aurelle (vers 70 ap. J.-C.), Lyon n°491, isolée de Porquerolles, et atelier de Sainte Croix à Fréjus (fin Ier-début IIe s. ap. J.-C.).

Tall amphora with a tapering spindle-shaped body ending in a long solid spike toe; narrow neck with everted rim and two short vertical handles set high. Bottom row shows dated provenance variants: Épave Lavezzi 2 (mid 1st c. AD), Lyon rue de la Favorite (early 1st c. AD), Épave Sud-Lavezzi 2 (ca. 22-25 AD), Camulodunum 186 A (2nd quarter 1st c. AD).

Ovoid-to-fusiform wine amphore produced at Marseille, with two handles, a flaring/collar rim and a narrowing lower body ending in a small ring/toe base. The illustrated example (Epave Plane 2) dates c. 410-380 BCE. The lower row of profiles shows the typological evolution: 2nd half 6th c. BCE (more biconical body), end 6th-5th-early 4th c. BCE, 4th c. BCE, 5th-3rd c. BCE, and 3rd-2nd c. BCE (progressively slimmer, more elongated body with smaller rims).

Slender, elongated fusiform amphora with a tall narrow neck, double or grooved handles running from below the rim to the shoulder, gently tapering body and a long solid spike toe. Bottom-row variants (Titan, Sud-Perduto 1, Tour Sainte-Marie, Pompéi) show the form's evolution from mid-1st c. BCE to before 79 CE.

Amphore à corps ovoïde/piriforme se terminant en pointe basse, col court à lèvre épaisse et deux anses arquées rejoignant l'épaule. Variantes illustrées : Plage de Camp Long (Agay, Saint-Raphaël) et environs du lac de Côme. Parfois confondue avec les Dressel 20 archaïques.
origin: Côte adriatique de l'Italie (région de Brindisi)

description: Amphore vinaire à corps allongé fuselé se rétrécissant vers une pointe pleine; col haut et étroit; anses bifides caractéristiques formées de deux boudins accolés. La fiche présente deux extrêmes morphologiques: un modèle long et effilé, l'autre plus court et trapu.

Amphore à corps ovoïde arrondi reposant sur un petit pied annulaire bas, col court avec lèvre marquée et deux petites anses verticales reliant le col à l'épaule. Production gallo-romaine de Narbonnaise. Variantes illustrées : Genève, Musée de Nyons (production locale ?), Lattes (demi-module).

Amphore vinaire à corps fuselé allongé, haut col cylindrique, lèvre épaisse, deux anses verticales sillonnées partant sous la lèvre, terminée par un pied plein en pointe. Variété précoce de plus petite taille dite Léetanienne 1. Imitée par certains ateliers du sud de la Gaule (Montans près de Gaillac).
origin: Tarraconaise (Espagne du Nord), région de Barcelone

description: Amphore à long col cylindrique avec lèvre développée, anses en boucle, corps fuselé/piriforme s'amincissant vers une longue pointe creuse. Variantes illustrées : Lyon rue de la Favorite (début Ier s. ap. J.-C.), épave Port-Vendres 2 (41-50 ap. J.-C.), Genève.

Amphore à corps ovoïde allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe basale courte; col court surmonté d'une lèvre épaisse débordante; deux anses en boudin reliant le col à l'épaule. Variantes illustrées : épave Grand Congloué 3 (milieu Ier s. av. J.-C.) et exemplaires isolés du golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres).

id: Amphore gauloise Amphore type Fréjus / Lenzbourg
description: Amphore à corps ovoïde sans pied distinct, terminée en pointe basse arrondie; col court avec lèvre éversée et deux anses courtes en boucle reliant la lèvre à l'épaule. Variantes en bas: exemplaires de Lenzbourg (fouilles du théâtre romain).

Amphore de transport étrusque à corps ovoïde se rétrécissant vers le bas, col court, lèvre marquée et deux anses verticales partant de l'épaule. Existe en petit et grand modèle. Variantes provenant des épaves de l'Estéou dou Miet (Marseille), Bon-Porté 1 (Ramatuelle) et d'une découverte isolée à Saint-Raphaël, toutes datées du VIe s. av. J.-C.

Petite amphore à corps ovoïde fuselé, col court à lèvre marquée, anses courtes en boudin reliant col et épaule, terminée par une pointe pleine. Variantes datées illustrées : Lyon rue de la Favorite (début Ier s. ap. J.-C.), épave Sud-Lavezzi 2 (env. 22-25 ap. J.-C.), épave Dramont D (milieu Ier s. ap. J.-C.).

Amphore élancée et fuselée au corps allongé, à col court surmonté d'une lèvre épaisse, anses verticales reliant col et épaule, et base se terminant en pointe pleine. Variantes datées du Ier s. ap. J.-C. produites à l'atelier de Saint-Cassien (Cannes); un exemplaire du Museum of London porte l'inscription peinte Liquamen Antipolitanum (sauce de poisson fabriquée à Antibes).

Ovoid-bodied amphora with a short neck, small everted rim, twin ribbed handles attached high on the shoulder, and a small flat to slightly pointed base. Used for wine. Bottom row shows dated provenance variants: Marseille (end 1st c. BCE), Fréjus quartier de Villeneuve (20-5 BCE), Fréjus demi-module atelier de l'Agachon (early 1st c. CE), and Lyon rue de la Favorite (early 1st c. CE).

id: Amphore de Bétique Amphore à saumure d'Espagne
description: Amphore fuselée à corps allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe pleine; col court avec bourrelet, deux petites anses verticales partant sous la lèvre. Variantes illustrées : épave du Titan (île du Levant, milieu Ier s. av. J.-C.), golfe de Fos et rade de Marseille (exemplaires isolés).

id: Amphore de Bétique Dressel 38 / Beltrán II A
description: Amphore à corps fusiforme/piriforme se rétrécissant vers une pointe pleine effilée, col court, lèvre épaisse et anses en boudin partant juste sous le bord. Variantes montrant un possible affinement de la panse au fil du temps (Lavezzi 1 vers 25 ap. J.-C., Planier 4, Tiboulen de Maïre env. 100 ap. J.-C.).

Amphore à corps allongé ovoïde, col distinct avec lèvre, deux anses, et petite pointe nettement détachée du fond de la panse avec un bouton de pâte faisant saillie à l'intérieur. Évolution montrée par variantes datées (Lyon début Ier s. ap. J.-C., épave Port-Vendres 2 41-50 ap. J.-C., épave Tour Sainte Marie milieu Ier s. ap. J.-C.).

Slender amphora with a tall narrow neck, ovoid-to-elongated body tapering steadily down to a long solid pointed toe; vertical rod/ear handles running from below the rim to the shoulder; thickened band rim. Bottom row shows dated provenance variants from the golfe de Fos and Alméria with slight differences in rim profile and toe form.

Amphore au corps ovoïde allongé se terminant en pointe (pied massif), avec un col court, deux anses verticales et une lèvre triangulaire peu développée. La série inférieure illustre des variantes provenant de l'épave de la Tour d'Agnello (Cap Corse).

Variante bétique : panse courte et trapue, pointe longue et conique nettement dégagée de la panse, anses longues implantées loin du col, embouchure large. Variantes illustrées : Golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres), épave Tiboulen de Maïre vers 100 ap. J.-C.

Variante lusitanienne : col plus court, contours plus arrondis, pointe dans le prolongement de la panse. Variantes illustrées : épave Cap Bénat 1 (Ier ou IIe s. ap. J.-C.) et Porto dos Cacos (Alcochete, Setúbal).

Small to medium wine amphora with ovoid body tapering downward to a small flat or rounded base, short narrow neck with everted rim and two short curved handles set high near the rim. Bottom-row variants from Marseille, the Petit Congloué wreck (10-30 AD) and Genève show similar profiles.
origin: Gaule narbonnaise (Languedoc, atelier de Corneilhan, et Marseille)

description: Amphore à corps allongé piriforme se rétrécissant vers une pointe pleine effilée (pointe creuse selon le texte), col haut et étroit, deux anses verticales en boudin reliant le col à l'épaule, lèvre saillante. Variantes datées illustrées en bas : épave Tiboulen de Maïre (Marseille, fin Ier s. ap. J.-C.), épave Chrétienne B (Saint-Raphaël), exemplaires isolés du Golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres).

Amphore à fond plat à panse ovoïde et col court avec lèvre épaissie; deux anses verticales reliant le col à l'épaule. Pâte dure et homogène, presque spongieuse, jaune très pâle en périphérie et grise vers le centre. Variantes datées: épave Sud-Lavezzi 2 (22-25 ap. J.-C.), épave Port-Vendres 2 (41-50 ap. J.-C.), variante d'un atelier lyonnais (La Muette, début Ier s. ap. J.-C.). À distinguer du type Oberaden 74 (Tarraconaise, col cylindrique, panse ovoïde moins large, anses arrondies à un sillon, fond plat).

Amphore ovoïde à corps galbé se rétrécissant vers une base étroite quasi pointue, col court à lèvre épaissie et deux anses verticales aux épaules. Variante de Cerveteri datée du 3e quart du VIIe s. av. J.-C. et exemplaire isolé au large de Syracuse.
Variante plus tardive à corps ovoïde élancé terminé en pointe, col court et deux anses verticales. Exemplaire de l'épave (?) Capo Graziano G (Lipari, îles Éoliennes), milieu du Ve s. av. J.-C.

Amphore à corps piriforme allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe basse solide; col court étroit avec lèvre légèrement éversée; deux anses verticales reliant l'épaule au col. Transportait des saumures. Variantes datées illustrées en bas : Épave Lavezzi 1 (vers 25 ap. J.-C.), Pompéi, et Musée de Villafranca del Penedés.

Amphore à saumure à long col, lèvre épaissie en collerette, anses verticales fines, corps fusiforme/piriforme se terminant par une pointe creuse allongée. Famille bétique non attribuable précisément entre Dressel 7 et 11. Variante illustrée en bas : autre amphore de l'épave de la Tour Sainte-Marie (Dressel 7-8 ?), corps plus élancé.

Petite amphore allongée, presque fusiforme, à corps cannelé/côtelé se rétrécissant vers une base pointue arrondie, col court avec deux petites anses; production de Lipari. Variantes datées 1a (Ier s. av. J.-C., Cassidaigne), 1b (Ier s. ap. J.-C., Rennes), 2a (IIe/IIIe s. ap. J.-C., Lipari), 2b (fin IIe/IIIe s. ap. J.-C., Londres).

Amphore vinaire à corps ovoïde/piriforme effilé se terminant en pointe, col court avec lèvre en bourrelet, deux anses verticales reliant l'épaule à la lèvre. Cross-réf. Agora K 114. Typologie en quatre variantes (Type A à D), du corps plus ovoïde et trapu vers des formes plus élancées et piriformes.
origin: Italie du Nord-Est (Forlimpopoli, province de Forlì)

description: Amphore de transport à corps piriforme/fuselé se rétrécissant vers un pied bas, col court à lèvre épaissie et deux anses verticales partant de l'épaule. Forme proche des amphores massaliètes anciennes et des dites « Corinthiennes B » fabriquées à Corcyre (Corfou). Variantes datées illustrées en bas : épave du Dattier (fin VIe s.), épave Bon-Porté 1 (Ramatuelle), Saint-Julien de Pézenas, exemplaires corcyréens (VIe–début Ve s. av. J.-C.).

Grande amphore cylindrique élancée à épaule arrondie, col court à lèvre épaissie, deux anses verticales et fond se terminant par un pied plein en pointe. Variantes datées : Tripolitaine I (Lepcis Magna et Pompéi, circule aux Ier-IIe s.), Tripolitaine II (Musée d'Atlit, Israël, circule du Ier au IVe s.) et Tripolitaine III (Lepcis Magna, circule du Ier au IVe s.).

Amphore à corps ovoïde allongé, col court à lèvre simple, deux anses courbes reliant le col à l'épaule, fond arrondi ou légèrement pointu. Variantes datées illustrées : Bérénice (Libye) et Pompéi (avant 79 ap. J.-C.).

Amphore allongée à corps cylindrique élancé, épaules arrondies, col court à lèvre épaissie, deux anses courtes attachées entre l'épaule et le col, terminée par une base pointue/pied solide. Variantes provenant de Barcelone (fin Ve-VIe s.), épave Porto A (Filicudi) et épave de la Palu (Port-Cros).

Amphore fusiforme à corps allongé orné de fines cannelures horizontales, terminé par une pointe effilée; col étroit. Une seule anse à la fin du Ier s., deux anses dès le IVe s. avec modification du profil du pied. Évolution illustrée par variantes: IIe-IIIe s., IVe s., Ve-VIe s. et VIe s.

Amphore globulaire à corps presque sphérique, col court avec lèvre épaisse, anses arquées robustes reliant col et épaule, base sans pied marqué. Variantes datées illustrées : Golfe de Fos (isolées) et Sainte-Colombe (milieu Ier s. ap. J.-C.).

source.item_label: Epave Saint-Gervais 3, Golfe de Fos, vers 150 ap. J.-C.

description: Small ovoid to piriform oil amphora with short neck, twin small ring handles set high on the shoulder, rounded body tapering to a low rounded/pointed base. Successor to the Dressel 20 for transporting Baetican olive oil from the mid-3rd c. AD. Illustrated provenances include the Golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres), the Trajan market deposit (Rome), Sud-Lavezzi 1 wreck (Bonifacio, late 4th–early 5th c.) and the Catalans wreck (Marseille, 4th c.).

Large cylindrical amphora with a tall slightly tapered body, short cylindrical neck with a band rim, two short oval handles set high, and a small solid spike toe. Also called 'Africano grande'. Bottom row shows dated provenance variants: Africaine II a (Tarragone, 180-280 AD), Africaine II b (Agay, 230-320 AD), Africaine II c (Golfe de Fos, 230-350 AD), Africaine II d (Epave Planier 7, 280-380 AD).

Amphore crétoise à corps ovoïde allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe basale, col court avec lèvre marquée et deux anses recourbées remontant au-dessus de l'épaule. Le type comprend des demi-amphores (11-12 l) et des quarts d'amphore (env. 5 l). Variantes illustrées : quart d'amphore d'Axos (Crète), quart d'amphore de La Canée (Crète), épave Alberti à Panarea (Iles Eoliennes), Pompéi (avant 79 ap. J.-C.) et Bérénice (Libye).

id: Amphore africaine Africaines cylindriques de grandes dimensions
description: Large cylindrical African amphora with tall tubular body, short narrow neck with everted rim, two small handles at the shoulder, and a small pointed toe. Drawn variants span Keay XXXV (380-450), Keay LV (450-550), Keay LVII (470-550) and Keay LXI (550-700), from wrecks at Dramont E, Tarragone, Golfe de Fos and Marseille.

Amphore très allongée et étroite, à corps fusiforme/en carotte se rétrécissant régulièrement vers une longue pointe pleine; petit col court à lèvre marquée et deux petites anses verticales à l'épaule. Une variété tardive plus petite pourrait être d'origine orientale; certains exemplaires du Dramont E contenaient des noyaux d'olives.

id: Amphore africaine Africaines cylindriques de moyennes dimensions
description: Medium-sized cylindrical North African amphora: long tubular body, short neck with everted/thickened rim, two short handles set high on the shoulder, and a solid pointed spike toe. Bottom row shows dated wreck variants (Pointe de la Luque B, Marseille, 4th c.; Pampelonne, Saint-Tropez, 4th c.; Dramont F, Saint-Raphaël, 2nd half 4th c.) differing in rim profile and body proportions.
Punic transport amphora with a sack-/pear-shaped body tapering to a rounded point, short cylindrical neck with simple rim and small ear-like handles set high on the shoulder.

source.figure_label: AMPHORE MAÑÁ A, MAÑÁ B, MAÑÁ C1b

description: Elongated, near-cylindrical Punic amphora with a tall body tapering to a point, short neck, simple rim and small loop handles at the shoulder.

source.figure_label: AMPHORE MAÑÁ A, MAÑÁ B, MAÑÁ C1b

description: Cylindrical Punic amphora with an elongated tubular body narrowing to a conical pointed base, short marked rim/neck and small handles set on the upper body.

source.figure_label: AMPHORE MAÑÁ A, MAÑÁ B, MAÑÁ C1b

description: Amphore globulaire à corps quasi sphérique, col court et étroit muni de deux petites anses, épaule marquée souvent décorée de cannelures horizontales. Variantes illustrées : Iatrus (Bulgarie), Tarragone (avant le milieu du VIe s.), Agora d'Athènes M 272 (fin IVe s.), côte ouest de la mer Noire.

Amphore au corps allongé se rétrécissant vers le bas, col étroit, lèvre plate et pendante à l'extérieur, anses courbes. Pâte fine rougeâtre à petits grains sombres ou clairs, engobe jaunâtre à noisette. Souvent confondue avec la Gauloise 4. Variantes illustrées : épave de la baie de Pampelonne (Saint-Tropez, IVe s.), Bougie (Algérie), Ampurias (avant fin IIIe s.), Bérénice (Libye).

Amphore au corps ovoïde à conique couvert de fines cannelures (rainures), col court avec anses arquées remontant du col à l'épaule, base arrondie sans pied distinct. Variante LR 1a au col étroit (Ve s.) et LR 1b au col plus large (VIe s.). Inscriptions peintes à symboles chrétiens fréquentes.
origin: Rives de la mer Noire, côte sud de la Turquie, Chypre, Rhodes

id: Amphore orientale Amphore de l'Égypte romaine
description: Amphore allongée à corps fuselé tapering vers une pointe basale; col long et étroit nettement marqué de fines nervures (rainures horizontales), avec deux petites anses verticales au sommet du col. Le type évolue vers une silhouette de plus en plus élancée; série de variantes datées du musée d'Alexandrie et du golfe de Fos.

Amphore au corps allongé, presque cylindrique à ovale, paroi à fines cannelures, épaule arrondie se terminant par une petite pointe basale; col court avec anses verticales courtes; pâte pincée par le potier au niveau de l'angle supérieur de l'anse. Variantes illustrées: Agora d'Athènes G 199 (début IIe s. ap. J.-C.), exemplaire isolé du golfe de Fos, Bérénice (Libye), Pompéi (avant 79 ap. J.-C.).
origin: Méditerranée orientale (Îles de la Mer Égée)

description: Elongated, near-cylindrical to slightly fusiform body tapering to a small solid spike/toe at the base; short narrow neck with simple rim and two small handles set high on the shoulder. Variants from several wrecks (Planier 7, Randello, Cabrera 3) show consistent slender profile.

Small-format version of the Dressel 20 olive-oil amphore whose profile evolves in parallel with the full-size type. Globular to spheroidal body, short neck with thickened rim, paired arched handles, small button/spike base. Drawings show the morphological evolution across dated find-spots: Oberaden (end 1st c. BCE, more ovoid), Lyon rue de la Favorite (early 1st c. AD), Port-Vendres 2 and Golfe de Fos (mid 1st c. AD), Tiboulen de Maïre Marseille (late 1st–early 2nd c. AD), Saint-Gervais 3 (mid 2nd c. AD) and Ostie (3rd c. AD, increasingly globular/flattened).

Amphore à corps allongé fusiforme se terminant en pointe, col haut surmonté de deux anses caractéristiques relevées en hauteur formant un angle marqué (anses 'à coude' ou 'à poucier'). Variantes datées illustrées en bas : Grand Congloué 1 (début IIe s. av. J.-C.), Anticythère (80-70 av. J.-C.), Lyon rue de la Favorite (premières années du Ier s. ap. J.-C.) montrant l'évolution de la forme et des anses.

Amphore élancée à corps fuselé se rétrécissant vers une pointe pleine; col cylindrique avec zone de cannelures; deux anses hautes en arc fortement coudées au-dessus de l'épaule. Variantes datées de Bagaud (Hyères), Ostie (Thermes du Nageur), Ostie IVe s., et Bérénice (Libye).

Amphore à corps piriforme/fusiforme se rétrécissant vers une pointe pleine basse; col court à lèvre simple, deux anses verticales reliant l'épaule au haut du col. Variantes d'épaves montrant des corps plus ou moins élancés et des pointes plus ou moins marquées.

Elongated ovoid body tapering to a pointed solid toe, short neck with thickened rim and two small handles. Difficult to distinguish from the Dressel 26 (thought to be a Campanian oil amphora). Variants illustrated from Rome and La Longarina (Ostie).

Amphore au corps allongé piriforme/fusiforme terminé par une pointe pleine, col court à lèvre simple, deux anses verticales reliant l'épaule au col. Variantes datées illustrées en bas (épave Sud-Lavezzi 1, IVe s.; épave Dramont F, fin IVe-début Ve s.).

Amphore élancée à corps ovoïde-allongé se rétrécissant vers une petite pointe basale; col court avec lèvre simple; deux anses verticales partant du col jusqu'à l'épaule. Variantes illustrées: Golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres), Chypre (coll. particulière), isolée rade de Marseille.
origin: Méditerranée orientale (Cilicie, côte sud de la Turquie)

description: Amphore fusiforme élancée à corps biconique se terminant en pointe; col cylindrique étroit surmonté d'une lèvre simple, petites anses verticales en boudin posées sur la partie haute du corps; surface partiellement striée. Variantes datées illustrées: El Tossal de la Cala (250-150 av. J.-C.), So N'Oms, La Vila Joiosa.

Petite amphore au corps conique allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe, épaule marquée, col court avec deux anses en boucle attachées sous le bord; paroi finement striée/cannelée. Variantes illustrées: exemplaire du Golfe de Fos (Musée d'Istres), exemplaire de l'Agora d'Athènes K 109, et découverte sous-marine au Liban.

Élongée à corps cylindrique allongé se rétrécissant vers le bas en une pointe pleine; col court avec lèvre épaissie et petites anses verticales attachées haut sur l'épaule. Variantes datées illustrées: Grand Congloué 2 (110-80 av. J.-C.), Golfe de Fos (isolée), Dramont A (Ier s. av. J.-C., épave contenant des olives).

Elongated amphora with a long narrow body tapering to a pointed toe, tall neck and twin vertical handles rising high above the rim. Body has an angular shoulder above a long fusiform-conical lower body. Several dated provenance variants illustrated (Kyrenia wreck, Cyprus, late 4th c. BCE; Alexandria Museum, c. 275 BCE; Koroni, Attica, c. 273-271 BCE).

Bag-shaped/piriform amphora with rounded body widest in the lower part, short narrow neck and two small loop handles set high on the shoulder; no distinct toe. LR5 fabric is sandy, powdery, beige to orange; LR6 fabric is hard-fired, red core with grey surface (often nearly metallic when overfired). Dated provenance variants illustrated: Athens Agora K108 (mid-3rd c.), Atlit (Israel), Ravenna (early 6th c.), Athens Agora M330 and M329.

Amphore à corps allongé fuselé se terminant par une pointe pleine, col cylindrique étroit et anses verticales souvent bifides remontant haut. Variantes datées illustrées en bas : Lyon (début Ier s. ap. J.-C.) et épave Dramont D / Saint-Raphaël (milieu Ier s. ap. J.-C.).
origin: Méditerranée orientale, sans doute île de Cos

description: Amphore à corps ovoïde/piriforme se terminant par un petit bouton ou toe pointu; col court avec lèvre épaissie, deux anses arquées reliant l'épaule au col. Variantes provenant de Rome et Vindonissa illustrées en bas.

Small piriform/pear-shaped amphora with an elongated body tapering to a narrow solid spike toe; short neck with everted rim and two short vertical handles set high on the shoulder. Bottom row shows dated wreck variants: baie de Pampelonne/Saint-Tropez (4th c.), Planier 7/Marseille (4th c.), épave chrétienne D/Saint-Raphaël (4th c.), Sud-Lavezzi 1/Bonifacio (late 4th–early 5th c.).

Petite amphore au corps ovoïde renflé, à col court surmonté d'une lèvre épaissie, deux anses courtes rejoignant l'épaule, et base arrondie sans pied marqué. Variantes datées illustrées : El Djem (Tunisie, à partir de la 2e moitié du IIe s.), Pompéi (avant 79, à partir du Ier s. ?), Leyde (Pays-Bas) et golfe de Fos.

Amphore fuselée à corps allongé se rétrécissant vers une pointe basale solide; col étroit cylindrique surmonté d'anses verticales. Illustrée par l'épave de la Tradelière (région de Cannes), fin Ier s. av. J.-C.
Amphore à corps ovoïde allongé terminé par une petite pointe, col cylindrique resserré et deux anses verticales. Origine presqu'île de Cnide (Turquie), IIe-Ier s. av. J.-C.

id: Amphore grecque Pompéi XIII / Agora G 198
description: Amphore à corps ovoïde-cylindrique se terminant en pointe basale, col court, anses verticales; estampille (KEΔ) sur l'épaule. Origine probable mer Égée, Ier-IIe s. ap. J.-C.

Amphore allongée à corps ovoïde/cylindrique sans col véritable, petites anses arquées sur l'épaule, lèvre peu marquée et base se terminant en pointe affinée. La forme évolue par allongement de la panse, affinement de la pointe, lèvre plus haute et épaules plus tombantes. Variantes illustrées : entre Atlit et Césarée (Israël, milieu Ve s.), Tarragone (entre IVe et milieu Ve s.), Ashdod (Israël), Musée d'Alexandrie, Ampurias.

Amphore allongée à long col tronconique évasé terminé par une lèvre en bandeau débordant, deux anses verticales partant de l'épaule, corps fuselé se rétrécissant en une pointe pleine. Variantes provinciales illustrées : Lixus (Maroc), Na Guardis (Majorque, fin IIe s. av. J.-C.), littoral d'Ibiza.

Amphore allongée à corps cylindrique étroit, épaules tombantes, col bas surmonté de deux petites anses verticales, paroi fréquemment cannelée, terminée par un fond pointu/conique. Variantes illustrées: Ampurias (Gérone), Costa del Penedès (fin Ve s. av. J.-C.), Épave Plane 2 (début IVe s. av. J.-C.), Épave Cabrera II (Baléares).
origin: Région de Carthage (Tunisie); Espagne du sud, Sicile (?), Sardaigne (?)

description: Amphore ovoïde à corps allongé et fond arrondi/pointu, col court avec rebord simple, deux anses verticales reliant col et épaule. Variantes provenant de La Canée (Crète, fin Ier-début IIe s.), Bérénice (Libye, fin IIIe s.) et Pompéi (avant 79 ap. J.-C.).

Small cylindrical-to-elongated amphora (type Africano piccolo) with a short neck, simple rim, small looped handles set high on the shoulder, slender tubular body and a small solid pointed toe. Drawn variants: Tipasa (Algérie, 2nd c. AD); Africaine I a (180-380 AD); isolated finds from the golfe de Fos; plus a limiting/borderline case for the type. Photo shows complete elongated vessel with footed toe.

Amphore allongée et fuselée à corps conique côtelé, col étroit, deux petites anses verticales hautes et base se terminant en pointe. Variantes illustrées : Tomi (Roumanie, Ve-VIe s.), Kellia (Egypte), Musée d'Alexandrie, Ravenne (fin VIe s.).

id: Amphore italique Agora M 302 / Keay LII
description: Petite amphore au corps ovoïde allongé, col court, deux anses verticales en boucle reliant l'épaule au col, fond effilé. Variantes provenant de Marseille (fouilles de la Bourse, milieu Ve s.), épave Dramont F et épave B de la pointe de la Luque (IVe s.).
origin: Sud de l'Italie (Calabre), peut-être Méditerranée orientale

description: Heavy outturned rim with a tapering lip and long handles bent sharply just under the rim; wide neck above a body that broadens toward the base, ending in a long spike that may be hollow or solid.
origin: Southern Spanish coast (e.g. Puerto Real, Cadiz; Punta Umbria, Huelva)

description: A simple rounded rim atop a cylindrical neck recalling Dressel 2-4; characteristic long single rod handles that rise to a sharp peak; body tapers to a solid spike that frequently bears slight corrugations.

Wine amphora with a short triangular rim, cylindrical body with rounded shoulder, long rod-like handles and a short stubby spike; frequently stamped on the rim (occasionally the neck) with two or three letters or a symbol such as an anchor or trident. Typically a rough, sandy, thick-walled fabric in light pink to light red tones.
origin: Italy (notably the Caecuban and Falernian Plains, with kilns in Campania, Latium and Etruria)

description: Small carrot-shaped amphora with a plain or rounded rim that usually lacks a neck, small thick loop handles, and a tapered body covered with horizontal rilling, ending in a point. Hard, rough, very sandy fabric in brick-red or grey, with well-rounded quartz and limestone grains.
origin: Uncertain; petrology suggests a desert environment, probably an unlocated Mediterranean source

description: Heavy thick rounded rim with short stubby semicircular ridged handles; body shows shallow horizontal ribbing often with wiped/brushed striations ('fettling'), terminating in a small solid spike. Fabric is thick and very rough, greenish-grey, packed with large rounded volcanic rock fragments (lava, volcanic glass, augite).
origin: Uncertain; volcanic western Mediterranean or possibly the Puy de Dôme region of France

description: Thick-walled bag-shaped amphora with a pointed spike or short stub base. Form A (Lamboglia 2) has a thickened slightly overhanging rim, triangular-to-squarish in profile, high cylindrical neck, thick oval handles, and a shoulder carination ending in a pointed spike. Form B (Buchi 6a) lacks the rim overhang, has round-section handles and a longer, more slender neck. Form C (Buchi 6b) is like B but has a curved rim and short stub base. Sometimes stamped on neck or rim. Fabric is fairly soft, smooth and slightly micaceous, buff to creamy buff with a pale orange core.
origin: A: Apulia; B and C: Istrian peninsula (Yugoslavia)
contents: Olive-oil and/or wine (also garum on B/C tituli picti)

description: Amphora with two strongly arched, heavy bifid handles whose peaks rise above the typically rounded rim; tall neck featuring a characteristic 'step', an elongated body and a plain button toe. Fabric is variable (several production centres); Benghazi examples are hard, sandy reddish-yellow with limestone, quartz and pyroxene inclusions.
contents: Not known (possibly wine, copying the Koan type)

description: Tall amphora with a high collar-like rim and narrow mouth, ribbed handles that curve in profile, an elongated spindle-shaped body ending in a short spike. Occasionally bears a stamp of two or three characters or a symbol on the rim. Often made in the distinctive Campanian 'black sand' fabric.
origin: Principally Campania (Italy), possibly Etruria; Spain also suggested
contents: Probably wine (olives also found in one Cavalière wreck vessel)
