Bowl similar to Form 80 but deeper, with a plain rim and plain flat base. Two variants: Type A with coarse rouletting over much of the exterior, Type B undecorated. A variant relates to Form 80B with thickened rim, curved wall, small flat base.

Small bowl similar to Form 71 but with a different rim; thin fine clay with thin smooth slip inside and over the rim. Broad fairly flat rim rising gently to a small knobbed or hooked lip whose inner face tends to be bevelled flat and slightly inset. Grooves common on outer and inner rim; centre may have rows of punched dots; top edge of lip sometimes with groups of small notches; outside occasionally grooved.

Large open dish/bowl in a bowl-like variant with a contracted floor and a longer, more flaring wall; rim sharply incurved and bevelled on the outside (nearly horizontal bevel), some pieces with a tall rim having a vertical outer face forming a sub-type. Generally rather thin-walled with good slip. Floor decorated with stamped motifs arranged in zones (star/rosette/palm and circle stamps) bounded by single, double or triple grooves. Rim diameter range c. 22-41 cm; very common.

Bowl/dish in fairly thick, less fine fabric with an upright lip set off from the rim by a broad concavity. Two variants: Type A has a plain (undecorated) rim top with the usual notches on the lip; Type B has a groove across the middle of the rim and a plain knobbed lip. Some examples have a circle or groove on the floor; one early piece has a curved body-profile and high lip without inner concavity. Mostly c.15-18 cm diameter, with smaller and larger variants.
Variant bowl with flaring wall and everted rim carrying rouletting on the outer lip.

Small bowl related to Forms 72-73 with a steep wall, thin medium-height foot and flat rim ending in a hanging lip. Exterior of the lip grooved; rim divided from lip by a concavity sometimes bearing rouletting; grooves on the floor, occasionally with a small recessed central knob. Fabric as Form 73, with a thin smooth to thicker more lustrous slip.

Dish with broad flat base, low curved wall and broad flat rim rising obliquely to a hooked lip; counterpart of bowl Form 72 sharing its rim type and fine fabric. Slight base-moulding combined with a groove forming a foot. Floor bears grooves and Style D stamped decoration (e.g. alternating palmettes and trefoil motifs in a band).

Shallow bowl with straight flaring wall curving in to a flat base of fairly small diameter. Rather fine-grained fabric with smooth surfaces and thick lustrous slip inside and over rim; low base-moulding with a groove on the underside set in from the edge. Type A has a plain rim set off by two grooves; Type B has a slightly thickened rim. Occasionally stamped.

Large dish with variable rim-forms (hooked, rolled, or simply thickened); decorated floor often with multiple grooves and one or two central circles. Stamped decoration occurs in several schemes: radiating palm-motifs with grooved/rouletted border (earlier, thin-walled, neatly rolled rims); alternating motifs in a broad band between grooves with undecorated centre (large close-packed stamps, grilles, chevrons); and a coarse simplified version with a single motif in a grooved band and thick lustrous slip. A late variant has a high rim flattened on top with heavy roll, reduced lower ledge, and a central cross-in-heart stamp.

Large bowl resembling Form 67 but with distinctive rim: a V-shaped hollow moulding topped by a broad flat member sloping up to a hooked lip; a groove at the lip and groove(s) or slight offset above the hollow moulding; mouldings bevelled flat. Good-quality finely granular clay with lime, brownish-red to maroon, well smoothed with thin matt slip inside and on upper exterior; sometimes 'twig-marks' under base.

Flat-based dish with curved wall and plain rim; base marked off from the wall by a slight moulding (not an inset), with a matching offset at the floor edge. Floor carries stamped decoration and grooves. Type A: brownish/maroon fabric with prominent lime particles, matt slip sometimes with twig-marks, normally shallow with sharply curving wall, Style B stamps and a double rouletted band; three size groups. Type B: finer orange-red ware with thin, smoothed slip, deeper with more sloping wall, Style C stamps.

Large plate with flat or gently sloping floor ending in an upright, roughly triangular rim that is bevelled flat inside and rounded below, the outer face bearing two or more grooves. Angular foot of fairly large diameter and medium height. Fine clean-breaking ware with smoothed surfaces and thin semi-lustrous slip inside and over the rim; groups of fine grooves and concave bands, sometimes rouletted, as decoration.

Large dish with a broad flat floor on a thin high foot set at the edge, with a steep curved wall ending in a thickened rim grooved on top. Feather-rouletting covers most of the wall; two or more grooves run along the rim top and usually a groove marks the base of the wall delimiting the rouletting. Floor bears grooves and stamped decoration (Style D), sometimes with a recessed central knob ringed by grooves. Fabric and decoration as Form 82.

Deep dish corresponding to plate Form 82; flat floor with sharp-cut foot near the edge, steep straight wall and projecting triangular rim. Rim exterior flat with two grooves and a rounded underside. Feather-rouletting covers the wall, sometimes with a groove at the bottom. Slight offset at the floor edge usually with grooves; floor bears stamped decoration (Style D) and groups of grooves. Late variants have sloping floor and more flaring wall approaching Form 82B.

Small rounded bowl with flat-topped rim and high thin foot; rouletting on exterior, grooves on rim and two grooves on floor. Type A: hemispherical bowl, thickened flat-topped rim, feather-rouletting over wall. Type B: incurved wall, heavier everted rim with two grooves, variable rouletting.

Large flat-based dish, shallower than Form 58, with a broad more-or-less horizontal rim stepped in two fasciae; the broader outer fascia has a groove or slight upward roll at the lip. Ware like Form 58B but often thicker/coarser; slip thick and semi-lustrous or thin and matt, with possible fine smoothing-marks. Stamped decoration enclosed by grooves usually on the floor. Type A has vertical gouging on the exterior wall (creating interior ridges); Type B has a plain wall.
Large open dish/bowl with a thickened, slightly incurved rim and sloping wall to a low base; profile of the earlier variant.
Deep open dish with everted/triangular rim and flaring wall to a low base; profile of the later variant.
Large flat dish with broad sloping floor and low everted/flange rim; floor bears rouletted decoration; low ring foot.
Large flat dish variant with plain sloping floor and low rim; low ring foot.

Large plate with flat floor and inset base like Forms 58-59; quarter-circular flaring rim rising from the floor edge. Groove at the lip, with stamped Style A decoration and grooves on the floor. A Lepcis Magna variant has an angular hooked lip. Apparently derived from Form 48.

Flat-based dish with a vertical wall that curves inward to meet the base and a plain rim; two grooves on the exterior below the rim, with stamped decoration (Style A) and grooves on the floor. Large and rare.
Rare large dish derived from Form 67 with similar body profile but a broad flat rim hooked at the lip; thick lustrous slip; floor carries Style A(iii) stamped decoration.

id: African Red Slip Ware Form 70 var
description: Variant dish with a curving wall and small rim carrying feathered/incised decoration near the lip.
Open dish variant with a curved flaring wall and flat base; simple rounded rim.
Shallow dish with curving wall; exterior decorated with grooves below the rim and oblique/incised strokes with small punched triangles.
Shallow flat-floored dish with low flaring wall and a thickened rim hooked at the base of the wall.
Open dish with curved wall rising from a flat floor; simple rim.
Open dish with a flattened/thickened rim and shallow wall; vertical hatched (rouletted) decoration near the rim.

Bowl resembling Form 96 but with a scalloped rather than rouletted rim. Rim flat to slightly convex and tilted down, edge scalloped into eight or ten slightly concave facets; one deep groove near the lip following the scalloping and a second groove near the inner edge. Stamped decoration (cross-monograms, animals, swastika, jewelled cross) at centre.

Shallow bowl with a broad, nearly flat floor, low curved wall and short flat rim, on a foot of medium height beneath the floor edge. Type A: medium-sized, floor decoration like Forms 96–97, small offset over the foot, flaring tapering foot meeting the wall at an angle. Type B: small, lacking offset or floor grooves, with a single central stamp.

Bowl with a sloping floor, a low vertical wall ending in a rolled rim, and a tall conical foot; interior lacks an offset. Decoration limited to grooves around the floor. Probably derived from Form 93.

Footed dish with shallow floor, low wall and a high stemmed foot flaring outward at the base; thick bright slip inside and on the upper exterior, the rest left rough with brush-marks. Some examples have a stamped cross at the centre within a groove.

Large bowl with a rounded body, flat rim carrying a heavy roll on its underside, and a knobbed foot of medium height; fabric tending to a pimply surface with thin dull slip; floor usually has two grooves, otherwise plain. Diameter about 27-30 cm.

Small bowl with a shallow floor rising to a low wall, a short thick flattened rim, and a rounded foot of medium height that curves smoothly into the body; rather poor fabric; undecorated. Estimated diameter about 16 cm.

Dish with a shallow curving floor terminating in a plain rim set off by a groove; flat base or low foot. Coarse gritty fabric with poor slip on interior and rim; floor decorated with continuous spiral burnishing.

Large serving-dish with shallow floor and heavy knobbed rim, general shape like Forms 104A and 105. Outer floor interrupted by a ring of fairly large circular bowl-shaped receptacles, each wheel-made and inserted, projecting below the floor line (originally about eight to ten compartments). Thick granular fabric with quartz inclusions; thick bright slip over interior and rim.

Large plate with a shallow sloping floor ending in a thick knobbed rim; rim usually flattened on top, convex outside, flattened and slightly hooked underneath, often squarish in section. Outer floor frequently stepped up by a chamfered band over the foot. Foot heavy and rounded, of medium height, higher on the outside than inside, sometimes set off by a groove. Thick coarse fabric with slip inside and over the rim; undecorated. Size D. 30-42 cm. Early variants (Form 90/105) noted.

Large plate similar to Form 105 but with a rolled rim; undecorated, with foot and floor treated as on Form 105. Diameter range about 32-39 cm; uncommon. One example shows no chamfer or groove on the foot and a flattened underside of the rim.
Large flaring dish with thickened/rolled rim and low foot; incised/stamped band of decoration on the floor near the wall.
Flaring dish with thickened rounded rim and low foot; rouletted marks on floor.
Large dish with curved flaring wall rising to a thickened rim and a low foot.
Medium-sized dish with a triangular or hooked rim bearing two grooves; wall sometimes coarsely rouletted (rougher than Form 84); grooves on the floor; no stamped decoration recorded.

Dish with shallow floor, low heavy foot and a knobbed or hooked rim flattened on the inside or top; thick granular fabric with heavy slip on inside and rim. Type A: fairly upright knobbed rim, flattened or concave inside, sometimes with burnished patterns or light central stamping plus grooves. Type B: elongated rim flattened on top, offset from the floor with a small hooked lip, grooves on floor. Type C: heavy squarish rim raised above the floor and downturned, flattened top, slight hook beneath.

Large dish with sloping floor, small angular foot and a broad thickened rim that continues the floor's slope; fine-grained fabric with smoothed surfaces and a thin lustrous slip on floor and rim; rim slightly convex inside with a small offset at floor junction and flatter outside with a stronger offset. Possibly a finer counterpart of Form 87B.

Almost hemispherical bowl with heavy rolled rim and flaring tapering foot. Type A is broad-based, foot diameter well over half that of rim, foot of medium height and fairly thin; steep wall with large heavy rim. Floor decoration like Forms 96-97: central stamp surrounded by a groove with a second groove round the floor edge.

Variant with reduced base (diameter not more than half the rim), more flaring wall and a low heavy, roughly triangular foot. Rim rather smaller. Stamped motif at centre of floor, sometimes with grooves as in Type A. Tends to coarser fabric with rough, brush-marked exterior.

Undecorated small bowl representing the latest stage of the series; an early variant (Delos example, max D. c.18.4) has a steeper wall, a low bevelled foot of small diameter, turning-marks on the underside and lower wall, an offset at the floor edge, no grooves, and a thick, slightly lustrous slip on the interior and rim only. Survives into the early 7th century.

Bowl with curved body and tall flaring foot; broad horizontal rim ending in an upturned hook at the lip. Floor set off from the wall by a small offset above the foot, with grooves on the floor surrounding a single central stamped motif (Style E).

Bowl similar to Form 95 but with a broad, slightly downturned rim covered with rouletting and slightly concave on top. Rather shallow sagging body, curved floor with offset at edge, tapering foot of medium height with slight outcurve at base. One groove near the floor edge and a central stamped motif (Style E) ringed by another groove. Granular clay with thick lustrous slip inside and over much of the wall, the rest self-slipped.
Deep dish with curved wall flaring to a heavy rim and low foot.
Large dish with strongly curved flaring wall, heavy rim and low foot ring.

Large open bowl with curving body, flat rim and a fairly high flaring foot; rather granular fabric slipped inside and on the rim. Usually a groove on the floor enclosing a single central stamp (Style E). Type A has a wide rim (2 cm+) often thickened at the lip, sometimes a high thin foot, thin dull pimply slip; Type B has a shorter rolled rim, coarser fabric with thick slip, heavier sometimes knobbed foot, and often a groove halfway up the outer wall.

Smaller version of Form 93; floor separated from wall by a slight offset above the foot. Type A has a broad downturned rim; Type B has a short rim, flat on top and rolled beneath, often with a groove on the wall. Diameters about 16-18.5 cm; uncommon.

Flanged form showing an evolution from Types A/B to D: early pieces have a wide flange (over ~2 cm) bevelled flat on both faces, meeting a hanging lip at a sharp angle, with a low slightly knobbed rim; later pieces have a taller rim and progressively smaller flange that reduces to a knob. Rolled/hooked flanges precede short flat ones. Floor rouletting (elaborate feather-rouletting in earlier types) shrinks to a single line as the flange diminishes; separate feet are an early trait, and fabric quality declines through the series.

Shallow flanged bowl related to Form 91, with a short tapering, markedly downturned flange; fine brownish fabric with thin smooth slip overall (akin to Form 68). Flat base, optionally moulded, with a groove near the edge; fine feather-rouletting covering most of the floor.
Shallow open bowl with incurved thickened rim and low ring foot; near-complete profile.
Open bowl with thickened rounded rim, gently curving wall with interior grooves and low ring foot.
Curved-wall bowl, thickened rim; variant marked 80B/99.

Small bowl with a gently incurving wall ending in a small thickened or outturned rim. Base not preserved on complete examples but probably high and flaring, like a reduced version of Forms 100–101. Undecorated.

Continuation: rim flattened on top with slight hook beneath, grooved underside; floor nearly flat and undecorated; foot variously high with mouldings, roulettings and grooves, or lower and plain. Type A linked to rectangular dishes of Form 56 with venatores/wild-beast motifs; Type B a later, related variant.

Open bowl/dish with a consistently high foot. Two variants: Type A has a broader, rolled or hooked rim with a thin high foot (some pieces stamped), while Type B has a shorter, thicker, slightly down- or up-turned rim, often with a groove along the lip and an external wall-groove; floors may bear one or two grooves and interior stamps (crosses, figures, animals, cantharus, cupid).

Large dish or bowl with a broad shallow floor, straight sloping wall and hooked or rolled rim. Floor slightly offset from wall, set on a fairly large foot of varying height. Decorated with stamps (Style E) and grooves on the floor, often a groove near the floor edge and occasionally on the wall. Thick granular fabric with smooth semi-lustrous slip inside and on rim; exterior self-slipped or rough with brush-marks. Type A has a steep wall, large bevelled hooked rim and fairly high foot; Type B has a more flaring wall, heavy rolled rim and low thick foot.

Large dish or bowl with sloping or curved floor ending in a heavy knobbed rim; foot of varying height; fabric as Form 103, usually thick. Typically a groove on the interior near the rim, stamped Style E(ii) decoration on the floor framed by two or three grooves, and an exterior groove about midway between rim and foot. Type A: shallow slightly curved floor, vertical rim rising well above floor and pointed top and bottom, medium flaring tapering foot often with slight knob. Type B: slightly deeper with more sloping floor, knobbed rim with less upward projection, low angular foot, heavier coarser fabric. Type C: shallow bowl with curved floor and rounded knobbed rim, body often recurved below rim, low triangular or square-cut foot of small diameter, no external groove, later examples unstamped.
Variant with a relatively angular rim and flange (one example less angular); thin, fine fabric. Interior may show grooves; rouletting on floor.
Flanged bowl with a broad band of feather-rouletting around the floor; some examples with more rounded flange and distinct foot.

Intermediate variant: rim like Type B but with a slightly narrower flange; base as Type C with a small groove beneath; band of rouletting narrower than on Type B. Some examples with feather-rouletting covering the floor, coarser ware with thick bright slip.

Fairly deep bowl with plain rim and a shorter, more rounded flange placed lower on the wall. Flat base with a low moulding at the edge and a broad groove on the underside. Narrow rouletted band on floor, sometimes reduced to a few lines in a slightly hollowed floor. Granular fabric with thick semi-lustrous slip inside and over flange; exterior often rough. Medium-sized, common.

Small, crudely made version of Type C with only a rudimentary flange. Base as Type C; two or three lines of rough rouletting inside. Ware as Type C but generally poorer quality. Rim diameter c. 12-15 cm.
Probable deep bowl with rounded body and slightly flaring rim, with an internal ledge where rim meets body; groove(s) on the outer rim. Bright slip inside and out.

Carinated handled form with a collar-like rim set slightly off from the body and a handle from rim to belly; a groove runs on top of the rim, a broad band of spiral rouletting covers the upper body, and the handle bears three grooves.
Slender curved profile; rim and handle like Form 138, with a groove along the top edge of the rim; broad band of spiral rouletting on the upper wall; handle bears about three grooves.

Round-bellied body with a slight shoulder carrying a collar-like rim; handle attached on the belly; decorated with rows of small indentations, sometimes with rouletting; handle has three grooves. Type A is broader-bellied with a low base-moulding in normal fabric; Type B is taller with a high base-moulding in thicker, coarser fabric, with a groove under the base edge and a leaf-band pattern of rouletting flanked by oblique indentations.

Dish with a wide flat base and a curved, roughly quarter-round wall that turns slightly inward at the rim. Interior burnished up to the rim; exterior wall often blackened or discolored from uneven kiln firing. A faint groove or offset marks the floor-to-wall junction. Early smaller variants with more flaring walls occur in Tripolitania.

Flattened domed lid with a hooked rim curved on the outer face; burnished on top; rim often discoloured outside; frequently a groove encircling the top where the curve begins down to the rim. Likely served as the lid for Form 181.

Two-handled flagon, including slender/elongated and broad squat variants as well as plain undecorated examples; typically decorated with paneled venatio scenes and acclamation mottoes (e.g. SINEMATI NIKA, TAVRISCI NIKA, TELEGENI NIKA, PENTASI NIKA), with applied figures, palm-branch and oak-branch dividers, and shell-motifs below the rim; handles bear leaf-bands or leaf-sprays; squat variant has broad mouth and small applique figures in a row round the body; undecorated examples have grooves below the rim and strap-like grooved handles.

Casserole in late Hellenistic tradition: shallow sagging base, slightly concave wall and broad flat rim; interior has a flat recessed band at the rim/wall junction to seat a lid, and an offset where floor meets wall. Mostly medium-sized, some smaller. Unslipped kitchen ware, often with grey-fired exterior; paired with lid Form 192.
cross_refs: CVA Univ. of Michigan 1 pl. XLV.21

description: Small jug with broad rounded belly, concave neck, and a flaring slightly rolled rim; grooved handle attached to the body; no decoration.

Spouted jug with ovoid body and a short flaring rim meeting it at an angle; angular handle running from rim to above the belly, rising over the rim and pressed into the lip; open semicircular spout with a heavy moulded lip rising obliquely from the rim opposite the handle; undecorated.
Rather slender curving vessel with a trefoil rim and a handle from rim to belly; related to Form 152.
Broad low biconical vessel with a narrow neck ending in a trefoil rim and a handle from rim to shoulder; rouletted decoration, with bands of rouletting on the shoulder and fine grooves on the neck.

Beaker with gently flaring, slightly curved sides and a small rim; low splaying foot; two handles running from rim to belly. Upper part decorated with rouletting or grooves; handles bear two grooves. A variant has a flat unmoulded base with a slight S-curved body.

Round-bodied bowl with slight shoulder and small rim-moulding, set on a stemmed foot that flares at the bottom. Small mould-made handles with relief decoration attached to the body. Fine thin fabric with smooth glossy slip outside. Applied figural motif at the centre of each side flanked by vertical motifs (palm-branches).
Lid matching Form 191; shallow dome with a plain rim bevelled on the outer edge, and a low flange on top shaped like a small inverted knobbed foot with a flat top surface.

Deep casserole with plain convex sides and a flat, slightly sagging base; small interior offset where wall meets floor; exterior wall often discoloured. Some examples have a grooved rim ('orlo bifido'). Not common.
Unslipped casserole version of Form 19; lacks feet and has no grooves on the underside; lid form unknown. Uncommon. Exterior tends to be discoloured/fired grey.

Large, fairly tall conically domed lid with a slightly thickened rim that is convex outside with an angle at the top; rim exterior usually blackened from kiln exposure. Type A has a small foot-like flange of narrow diameter on top (like Form 192 but less crisp); Type B has a plain rounded top. Possibly served as lids for casseroles of Form 23.

Casserole with roughly vertical wall and rounded bottom; heavy convex rim-moulding with a small internal seating to take a lid. Underside has small grooves/ridges (as Form 23); interior wall similarly treated, often with a 'stepped' look. Exterior of rim and wall frequently blackened.
Wide low body with broad shoulder; tubular neck ending in a funnel-shaped rim; small low foot. Two broad strap handles running from the neck/rim junction to the shoulder edge. Plain, undecorated.
Ovoid body with an offset concave neck and heavy moulded rim; tall base-moulding incorporating a low foot. Mould-made handles bearing a herringbone relief pattern. Undecorated body.

Two-handled flagon with ovoid body on a broad flat base; tall bulging neck with a small rim moulding. Handles run from neck to body and are mould-made with faint decoration. A single groove beneath the base edge. Fairly fine fabric with a dark slip.
Unslipped lid like Form 182, with a low domed top and an upward-hooked rim; gently convex top encircled by two grooves, often blackened on the outer surface. Uncommon.

Inkwell with a slightly convex top pierced by a large central opening encircled by a small overhanging lip, plus a small secondary hole to one side; low rim around the edge. Body profile variable: one type deep with vertical sides curving in at base on a low foot; another shallower and splaying with flaring sides, flat base with edge moulding and a groove defining a slight foot.
Cruet with globular body and flat moulded base; narrow neck fitted with a filter at its base and a small loop arching over the mouth.

Spouted jug with globular body, flat moulded base and a slightly flaring neck with flattened rim. Grooved handle runs from rim to body ending in a rat-tail; a short tubular spout sits on the shoulder at right angles to the handle. A strainer with five holes in quincunx arrangement spans the base of the neck; neck interior unslipped.

Smaller, finer counterpart of Form 183 with short rims (concave, sloping or flat); some variants in thin fine ware with glossy vermilion slip, with the wall bulging near the bottom and a small everted rim. Made in the same workshops with a similar distribution.
Casserole lid matching Form 183, in similar coarse fabric. Shallow domed profile with a low flat knob and a thickened rolled rim; surface shows line-burnishing on top.
Goblet with a tall ridged solid stem carrying a small bowl with slightly incurving sides; broad flat base resting on a low ledge-foot around the edge, with grooves under the rim and on the underside.

Wide, low vessel with a slack sagging body and a small moulding at the rim; a handle springs from the body and carries two grooves; body bears rouletted (often spiral) bands; a variant has indentations instead of rouletting.
Comparatively slender, high-bellied vessel with a short outward-flaring rim and a handle on the body; decorated with bands of rouletting, with grooves on the handle and in the handle-zone.
Small version of Form 131 with a wide sagging body; handle bears a central groove; without decoration.
Small jar-shaped mug with a low bead rim and flat base; handle set on the body; some examples show a groove around the shoulder and grooves on the handle.

Nearly globular body with a short flaring rim grooved at the lip; handle folded into a small loop at the top and marked with several grooves; one example has indentations on the body. Handle form seems to imitate glass vessels.

Closed feeder-vase in early fabric, slipped on the exterior only. Biconical body with a wide mouth and slight rim, a strainer set across the mouth. Flat base with a pronounced base-moulding and a groove near the edge marking off a small foot; raised fillet on the lower body near the base. Grooved ring-handle on the upper body with a short spout at right-angles to it.
Rounded deep cup with a tubular spout set on the body and a single curved handle opposite; low foot.
Open flaring bowl with curving walls rising from a small foot; oval decorative motif on body.
Tall ovoid two-handled vessel with narrow mouth and elongated body tapering to a small base.
Globular spouted jug with a long tubular spout and a high arching handle from rim to body.
Small squat jug with rounded body, short neck and a small loop handle.
Ovoid mug/jug with everted rim and a single loop handle on a small foot.
Round-bellied vessel with a broad concave neck and a flat-topped rim carrying a double moulding; slight ridge where body meets neck; decorated with rouletting and a small groove above the belly.

Small globular-bodied form with a tubular neck and downturned rim, a handle running from neck to belly, and rouletted lines on the upper body; larger variants may have a low base-moulding and strap handle.

Saucepan-type patera; flattened handle with mould-made relief on upper surface—shallow fluting ending in a flattened lion's head, with a small rosette and cross-grooves at the junction; flat undecorated underside. Imitates metal paterae with fluted animal-head handles.

Slender curving jug with narrow flat-rimmed mouth; angular ungrooved handle running from rim to belly, ending in a 'rat-tail'; small knob-like projections flanking the handle on the rim; undecorated. Imitates a metalware shape.

Curving jug with wider mouth; slightly outcurved rim with a small upward hook at the lip; curving handle from rim to belly; undecorated. Close to a silverware form from the Casa del Menandro hoard at Pompeii, suggesting a Flavian date.

Shallow domed flanged lid with a flat solid knob; a simplified version with a short rim. Appliqué ornament around the top; fine fabric slipped only on the upper surface. Probably served as the lid for a bowl form. Rare.

Pilgrim-flask with a flat circular body, lentoid in section, made from two wheel-thrown halves joined together; short narrow wheel-made neck with a flaring, usually bell-shaped mouth, and two angular grooved handles set on the edge. Often decorated with rouletting lines or a groove encircling the body, matching on both faces.
Deep bowl with vertical thickened rim, straight wall and flat base, grooved decoration below rim.
Domed lid with sloping wall and flanged edge, banded decoration.
Deep bowl with everted thickened rim, curving wall and flat base.
Wide-mouthed vase with a sagging curved body, heavy moulding at the rim and a low foot; two handles running from just below the rim down to the belly. Decoration follows the scheme of Form 172.
Pear-shaped jug or flagon with a cup-shaped mouth, body resembling Form 171; handle(s) run from the mouth/body junction to the belly. Occurs in one- and two-handled versions. Rare.

Flask with a sagging ovoid body and small rim-moulding (like broader Form 171), topped by a tall tubular neck with two sets of grooves and slight moulding at the lip; no handle. Decoration of three figured motifs (each with a diadem above) alternating with three vertical palm-branches.

Small flask shaped like the smaller versions of Form 174 but lacking a handle; small cordon on the neck below the disc. Decoration includes a charging boar, palm-branch, spiked wreath and palm-branches.

Small two-handled flagon with globular body and long tapering neck; small rim-moulding and base as on Form 171; two S-curved handles running from the lower neck to the body; two grooves on the upper neck; decorated on each side with one or two figured motifs flanked by vertical palm-branches or similar. Height roughly 11.5-18 cm. Common.

Round-bellied vessel with a long narrow neck closed at the top apart from a small opening, set on a low delicate foot; base pierced to act as a strainer; mould-made handle running from neck to body bearing relief decoration, with a central ridge flanked by oblique strokes. Fine thin fabric with smoothed glossy surfaces.

Mug with a sagging 'bag-beaker' type body, a small moulding at the rim, and a grooved 'sliced' handle attached on the body; slip applied to the exterior only and flat base. Some examples show roulette lines on the body and tend toward a more globular shape.

Handled vessel with a sagging, sometimes carinated body and a short outturned rim; a handle runs from rim to belly. The belly bears one or more grooves, usually accompanied by rouletting; the shape is quite variable (one example of 'bag-beaker' type).
Small two-handled flagon similar to Form 172 but with a tall neck made of a tubular, spirally grooved spout set on a wider plain lower section, separated by a disc; handles join the lower neck. Rare.

Broad-bellied jug with a slight shoulder and long neck carrying a disc on its upper part, set on a low simple foot of fairly wide diameter; single handle from lower neck to shoulder, often with two decorative bands. Sometimes minor offsets or grooves at the neck base and grooves below the disc. Decoration resembles Form 171, with two alternating main motifs and three vertical dividers. Common.
Small flask with a rounded globular body and flattened shoulder, set on a low foot; short tubular neck that flares slightly toward the mouth. One decorated example known.

Slender, curving jug with a narrow neck and heavy collar-like rim; handle running from the rim base to the shoulder; apparently flat-based. Mould-made relief decoration covers body and neck, divided into tall narrow panels by vertical herringbone ridges, with animals, lozenges and palm-trees.

Feeder-vase with roughly cylindrical, horizontally fluted body and a closed domed top; a projecting filling mouth on one side, a small spout on the other, and a loop-handle across the top. Type A has an angular slightly concave body widening downward on a low foot; Type B has a more rounded body with vertical sides and a flat moulded base.

Askos with an elongated, bird-shaped body; a short constricted front spout with bell-shaped mouth rising nearly vertically, a small horizontal tubular spout at the rear, and a grooved handle along the top. Small flat base with a high external moulding; body wheel-made in one piece and pulled into an oval form leaving a seam along the top. Spouts and handle added separately; one example has a front spout modelled as a bird's head.

Deep casserole with flat or sagging base, roughly vertical wall and a short concave rim. Thick gritty fabric, seemingly unslipped; exterior burnished while interior and rim-top left rough. Clay deep pinkish-red to maroon, burnished surfaces brownish-red.
Variant resembling Form 183 but shallower, with a small bead-rim like Form 184; normal coarse fabric.

Curving-profile flagon lacking a pronounced rim; two handles run from just under the rim to the top of the belly, ending in 'rat-tail' terminals below. Variants show plain inward-hooked lip with ungrooved convex handles, or a flat-topped rim with slight external moulding and a small cordon below the rim with a longer neck.
Sagging, curved-bodied flagon with a flaring rim and a slight groove below the lip; handles like those of Form 161 but grooved (two grooves on the handle).

Large open jar with tall vertical walls, a shallow rounded base and a short overhanging rim bearing a slight internal ledge, probably for seating a lid; wall has faint ribbing with pronounced wheel-marks inside and a smooth bottom.
cross_refs: Almagro, Las necropolis de Ampurias ii, fig. 154 no. 15

description: Large open jar with tall vertical sides, rim and base treated as on Form 197, and shallow ridges on both the interior and exterior of the wall.
Thin-walled bowl with curved wall and plain rim; flat base with a low moulding; vertical indentations on the lower wall, with fine grooves below the rim and beneath the base edge.

Thin-walled conical beaker on a low foot; wall bears two or three rows of small stamps (lozenges or planta pedis) alternating with bands of rouletting, framed by grooves or small cordons; small moulding or convex moulding at rim.

Wide body with a double bulge, a narrow neck topped by a tall bell-shaped rim; mouldings at the lip, base of rim and base of neck; a high-arching grooved handle running from neck to shoulder; no decoration.

Double-convex body with the upper bulge smaller than the lower; tall screw-neck (plain vertical lower part, contracted upper part with spiral grooving) ending in a slightly flaring mouth; flat base with a fairly high edge moulding; high-arching handle from lower neck to shoulder edge with a single central groove; fabric generally coarser than related forms.
Deep bowl/basin with incurved plain rim and a band of impressed/rouletted decoration on the upper exterior; flaring lower wall to a small base.
Shallow flaring dish with a hooked/upturned rim and shallow rounded floor; band of short vertical strokes near the base on the exterior.

Dish with flat base, outward-flaring wall and a thickened rim that is bevelled or rounded externally, occasionally slightly incurved. Variants include one with a low foot (grooves around the floor centre) and one with a heavy knobbed rim bearing stamped decoration.
Dish with hooked/beaked rim and curving wall; band of impressed strokes on the floor near the base.
Dish variant with everted/hooked rim bearing a band of short impressed strokes on the exterior and a flaring wall to the base.
Rim and wall fragment with hooked rim and curving wall (smaller variant).
Bowl with incurved/plain rim and steeply curving wall to a small base.
Small bowl whose rim is broad and flat with an overhanging lip, grooved across the top surface.
Plate with a heavy upturned rim; version A has a knobbed rim, rounded underneath. Base form not preserved; underside shows multiple rouletting.
Plate with a heavy upturned rim; version B has a tapering, near-vertical rim of roughly triangular section. Base form not preserved.
Dish standing on a low foot, with sloping wall and an upright hooked rim; rouletted decoration on the wall and grooves on the rim.
Small bowl with a flat-topped rim, rounded wall and a fairly tall foot; most of the exterior is rouletted.

Dish with flat base, sloping wall and broad flat rim, in three versions: A with a hooked lip grooved on top; B with a hanging lip sometimes rouletted outside; C with a plain lip grooved on top. Floor sometimes stamped (e.g. foot motifs).

Shallow bowl with a broad hooked rim that is 'stepped' on top; low 'double' feet probably belong to it. A variant is a deeper version with a shorter stepped rim, slightly hooked and rouletted outside. Some bases carry stamped decoration.

Deep open bowl/basin with a straight wall flaring at roughly 45 degrees, a heavy angular rim and a low, thick foot. Early pieces are deeper with a tall steep wall and short flat rim (slightly concave/offset beneath); later examples are more open and flaring with a shorter, squarer rim and tend to be smaller. Deep counterpart to the Form 2 dishes.

Small to medium dish with a shallow flaring wall ending in a plain or thickened rim, and a low heavy foot (as on Form 1) frequently hollowed underneath. Develops from a larger earlier-2nd-century type with higher wall and small rim-moulding (sometimes a floor groove) toward a smaller, shallower, plainer and more carelessly made late version. Second-century diameter c. 20-25 cm, late examples c. 18-20 cm.

Medium to large dish with shallow curving floor and incurved wall, a slight angle on the exterior at the wall/floor junction, and a triangular tapering foot of fairly wide diameter (chamfered outside, vertical inside); floor sometimes grooved. Fabric tends to contain silvery mica with a dull gloss.
Small bowl with an upright wall, the bowl counterpart of the Form 4 dish; rare, poorly finished.
Hemispherical bowl with a flange below the rim and a low, heavy foot; develops from an earlier vertical-rimmed version, here with a lower, more splayed rim that tends to merge into the flange.

Dish/bowl with sloping, curved or near-straight wall and a low foot; rim knobbed or flattened, rounded externally and concave beneath, with a small offset where it meets the wall. Inside generally rough with fine brush-marks; a few early pieces have stamped decoration. Successor to Form 3. Three variants: A heavy knobbed or squarish rim; B slightly elongated rim rounded on top, sometimes hooked; C elongated rim flattened or concave on top, slightly everted.
cross_refs: Waagé Antioch iv.i pl. XI shape 949u
Waagé Antioch iv.i pl. XI shape 949a

description: Large dish/bowl form classified by a series of rim variants. Type D: lower rim bulges out into a thick roll, usually with triple deeply-impressed rouletting outside (uncommon). Type E: continuation of C, rim still vertical but with greater overhang at base, flat or concave underside slightly offset from wall, often one or two rouletted lines outside. Type F: continuation of D/E, lower more projecting rim, exterior concave or rolled, broad flattish underside offset at wall junction, sometimes deep rouletting outside. Type G: like F but flat to slightly convex outer face with matching internal hollow, no rouletting. Type H: heavy triangular rim, with or without offset on underside, sometimes a single line of rough rouletting outside, thicker coarser fabric with thick glossy interior slip. Floor decoration includes stamped motifs (circles, lions, lioness, floral, cross) in zones bordered by grooves and rouletting; rims often carry multiple lines of rouletting. Small versions tend to be early.
cross_refs: Waagé Antioch iv.i pl. XI shape 944u

description: Carinated bowl with a broad downturned tapering rim that is concave on top and carries ridges or grooves (usually two small ridges); small foot, sometimes a slight offset on the underside where rim meets wall; interior often rough with fine brush-marks and no stamped decoration. A variant has a single central groove on the concave rim with an offset underneath.
Small plain dish with a vertical rim, flat floor and a bevelled foot of medium height; resembles Form 1 in shape but is unrelated.

Dish with curved body and a broad, horizontal rim that is slightly concave above and thickens to a bevelled lip; low foot, stamped decoration on the floor. Two variants: Type A has a shorter, thickish rim with slightly rounded underside; Type B has a broader rim, slightly concave below and set off from the wall by a small offset, sometimes with rouletting on the upper face and a deeper body. Small undecorated versions also occur.
cross_refs: Waagé Antioch iv.i pl. X shape 913k

description: Dish with shallow curved body and broad flaring rim flattened on top; flat base hollowed underneath to form a false (or low turned) foot. Often underfired with orange tone and discoloured rim edge. Stamped decoration on larger pieces. Three types: A large with stamped floor decoration in one or two zones each within a shallow groove (D. c. 27-38); B medium/small undecorated with narrower, sometimes convex rim and occasional lip groove (D. c. 16-24 and c. 11-14); C rare variant of B with rim continuing the wall line and stepped into two flat bands on top.

Dish with a fairly tall vertical rim that tends to incurve at the lip; shallow curved floor; tapering foot of medium height chamfered on the outside; slight carination where rim meets the underside; undecorated.
Dish with a similar or somewhat lower vertical curved rim; low foot of the ordinary type; shallow curved floor; undecorated.

Dish with a curving floor ending in a thickened rim that incorporates a small flange; base hollowed to form a false foot (like Form 2). Floor bears stamped decoration (band of palmettes between two shallow grooves). Rare, possibly an early variant of Form 3.

Dish/bowl form with several variants: a curved-wall version (Type C) having a plain, slightly thickened rim with rouletting on the rim exterior, and a small shallow version (Type D) with a curved wall, plain rounded rim and low foot, left undecorated. Type A is the direct successor of late Candarli ware Form 4, sharing its general profile and foot treatment, with some examples showing transitional fabric (glossy interior slip and discolored exterior rim).

Shallow bowl/deep dish with curved body and low foot resembling Form 3; heavy knobbed rim that is flattened on top and chamfered beneath, with a slight offset where it meets the wall; stamped motif at floor centre. A small undecorated version also exists.

Dish with a low steep wall and short outturned rim carrying a small flange on top along the inner edge. Associated dish bases have high, slightly knobbed feet, usually with a single stamped motif at the floor centre.
Shallow bowl with thickened rim, grooved wall and low foot.
Small deep bowl with incurved rim and ring foot.

id: Late Roman C Ware Type G
description: No complete examples known for the standard form. A deep variant has a tall curving wall and a low foot of small diameter, with a stamped cross motif at the floor centre.
cross_refs: Waagé Antioch iv.i pl. XI shape 947a

id: Late Roman C Ware Type H
description: Early examples resemble Type C, with a concave undecorated rim and a central stamped motif of paired volutes within a circle. The normal version carries a single band of rouletting on the rim and a ring of palmette-and-volute stamps around the floor.

id: Late Roman C Ware Type C
description: Shallow dish with round-topped, flat-topped or chamfered rim, sometimes a line of rouletting on the outside; central stamped decoration only (cross, cross-monogram with pendants, stag, or hares), occasionally with grooves around the floor. Diameter roughly 15.5-27 cm.
cross_refs: Sellers and Baramki, BASOR Suppl. Studies 15-16, fig.30.3

id: Late Roman C Ware Type D
description: Fragmentary dish with a triple line of deep rouletting on the rim; probably a single stamp at the centre (now missing). Estimated diameter about 32 cm.

id: Late Roman C Ware Type E
description: Shallow dish with bevelled foot and a slightly projecting rim with a small offset on the underside; one line of rouletting on the rim. Central stamped decoration such as paired birds (peahens beak to beak), a running 'lioness', or a cross-monogram with pendants. Diameter roughly 25-35 cm.

id: Late Roman C Ware Type F
description: Dish with a low rim rounded on top and nearly flat on the outside and underside, no rouletting; floor stamped with crosses, probably originally three set side by side. Estimated diameter about 24 cm.
cross_refs: Robinson, Athenian Agora V, M 351, pl.36

description: Dish with a wide flat base and flaring wall ending in a thickened upright or incurved rim that is convex outside and juts out at the wall junction. Base finished with a low ledge-foot or groove around its edge. Wall bears one or two bands of short light rouletting, sometimes a stamped motif in the floor centre, and commonly a single short wavy incised line on the rim exterior. Variety A: plain rim, low ledge-foot (early); Variety B: plain rim, flat base with a shallow groove near the edge; Variety C: rim with two exterior grooves, base as B.

Basin with steeply flaring walls and a flat base; slightly thickened rim rounded inside, often with a flat moulding outside (later examples with knobbed or hooked rims). Two short, heavy round-sectioned horizontal handles set just below the rim, pinched at the center for grip. Exterior wall frequently shows close irregular, stepped ridging. Slip usually partial, covering interior and rim zone.

Broad-bodied two-handled jar with a low hollowed-out foot; rouletting on the lower body and handles bearing a broad central groove. Slip covers most of the exterior and the inside of the neck. Known from a single example.

Large deep basin, essentially a deep version of Form 9C; grooved sharply inturned rim, flat grooved base, irregular rouletting; sometimes a wavy line on the rim. A variant has steep straight sides, high triangular rim and a slight foot. Uncommon.

Open dish or bowl with straight outward-splaying walls and a flat rim that ends in a small upturned hook; rouletted decoration on the exterior. Known only from fragments and uncommon. A shallow variant has a low foot like Form 3.2.

Small bowl with shallow curved wall and flat base; rim is thickened and triangular. Undecorated, though a few have a wavy-line on the outside of the rim. Often roughly made with exterior wheel-ridging and wire-drawn bases. Diameter c. 14-19.
cross_refs: Waagé Antioch iv.i 53 pl. X shape 930u

description: Dish or bowl with a curving floor and upcurved rim slightly hooked on the inside, with two grooves on the exterior; rouletting on the underside. Estimated diameter c. 30. Rare, known from fragments only.
Thick-walled basin with a heavy rectangular rim grooved on top and set off from the wall on the outside by an angular offset; rouletting on the exterior. Diameter c. 30-40. No complete examples.
Shallow bowl/dish with rounded body and incised grooves on the interior wall near the rim.
Large open bowl with thickened curved rim; exterior wall decorated with bands of rouletted/stamped ornament.

Shallow open dish imitating African Red Slip Form 84, with rouletting on the wall and stamped decoration (motifs akin to African Styles A-D); low hollowed Cypriot-type foot. Normal type rather shallow with a crude knobbed rim; some examples bear grooves and a short incised wavy line on the rim. Small versions and debased (poorer-fabric) versions occur, plus a large variant (Form 1/2) and a piece transitional to Form 9.
cross_refs: Waagé Antioch iv.i pl. X shape 930k

description: Dish with steep wall bearing rouletting and a knobbed, grooved rim; floor and foot like Form 1. Floor often carries stamped decoration (palm-branches, pomegranates, circle-motifs, almond-shaped stamps and trefoils) framed by grooves. Sizes mostly D. c. 22-29.5, with a smaller version 15.5-19.

Small bowl related to Form 2 with curved wall and a foot of varying height; rim thickened or knobbed, sometimes grooved; one or two bands of rouletting on the exterior. Development runs from a deeper form with grooved rim to a shallower one with plain knobbed rim. Not stamped. D. c. 14.5-19.
Dish or bowl with sloping wall and flat rim carrying a row of punched knobs; rouletting on the exterior below the rim and a groove on the rim at the lip. Rare, with no complete examples.

Small flagon with rough incised patterns on a flat shoulder; flat grooved base with external moulding and a small cordon at the base of the neck; handle attached at the rim. Represents an intermediate developmental stage of the type.
Squat narrow-mouthed bottle with a rounded bottom and short neck.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form L
description: Small dish with a sloping floor and a thickened, grooved rim; a reduced version of Forms H-I; uncommon.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form M
description: Dish shaped like Form J but with a grooved, thick angular rim; undecorated. Treated as a variant of Form J2.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form N-O
description: Small bowls with short overhanging rims and either low feet or flat bases; undecorated.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form P
description: Bowl imitating African Red Slip Ware Form 99; undecorated.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form Q
description: Flanged bowl modeled on earlier versions of African Red Slip Form 91; flat-based, in large and small versions, some reportedly stamped. Probable predecessor of Form U.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form R
description: Bowl with a flat rim hooked upward at the lip and a low foot; compared to African Red Slip Form 95.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form S
description: Open bowl with a low foot and a wide, angular flange; found together with an example of Form HH.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form T
description: Small flat-based bowl with a flange set about midway up the wall.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form U
description: Flanged bowl copying African Red Slip Form 91; a later development of Form Q. Usually small, with a low foot and undecorated; a larger rouletted variant also occurs, sometimes closely copying Form 91C with a flat grooved base and drooping flange.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form V
description: Small to medium bowl with a small flange and coarse rouletting on the outer rim, set on a low foot; the standard late member of the flanged-bowl series. Two common variants: a low-rimmed type with a single rouletted line, and a high-rimmed type with multiple rouletting and often a groove at the lip.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form A
description: Deep bowl with vertical sides bearing wall-mouldings and a low foot; occurs only at the Monastery of Epiphanius, A being early in that sequence.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form B
description: Deep bowl with vertical sides bearing wall-mouldings and a low foot; from the Monastery of Epiphanius, later in the sequence than A.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form C
description: Bowl whose wall curves up to a vertical rim, set on a low foot; rare.
cross_refs: Griffiths, LAAA xiv (1927) pl. LIX 15 = LX 16

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form D
description: Deep bowl with inward-sloping wall and low foot, decorated with rouletting; early.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form E
description: Deep bowl or beaker with near-vertical wall and high foot, rouletted; rare.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form F
description: Dish with upcurved rim and high foot, undecorated; uncommon.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form G
description: Similar dish to F but with low foot and variable rim angle; small to medium, sometimes with stamps and rouletting.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form H
description: Dish/plate with shallow sloping floor and heavy upright overhanging rim on a low foot; usually with stamped decoration.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form I
description: Dish/plate with shallow sloping floor and heavy upright overhanging rim on a low foot; usually stamped, related to H.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form J
description: Deep dish with carinated wall offset at the edge of the floor and a heavy knobbed or tilted rim on a low foot; three variants - (1) early, with stamped decoration enclosed by floor rouletting; (2) later, undecorated; (3) late, small bowl-like version of (2).
Shallow open dish with low flaring wall and a simple slightly thickened rim; copies an African Red Slip dish of late 4th/early 5th c. with stamped decoration of 'fringed circle' motifs.
Bowl with curving wall rising to a near-vertical rim on a low ring foot; imitates African Form 93, with a stamped cross at the centre of the floor.
Bowl with flaring wall and everted rim on a low foot; imitates African Form 93, with a stamped cross at the centre of the floor.
Small bowl with curved wall and outturned rim on a low ring foot, copying later African dish types (Forms 82–84).
Shallow open form with curving wall and incurved/grooved rim; horizontal grooves below rim and a row of small impressed ovals on the wall.
Shallow bowl fragment with simple plain rim and curving wall.
Large shallow dish with low ring foot and flaring wall; rouletted/notched band on exterior rim and incised hatched decoration on the wall.
Large flat plate/dish with broad flaring floor, thickened flat rim and low splayed ring foot.
Large shallow bowl with deeply curving wall and simple rim, low rounded base.
Bowl rim fragment with curving wall; rouletted/notched band on the exterior near the rim.
Small bowl rim fragment with curved wall and slanting impressed/incised decoration below the rim.
Carinated bowl with flaring upper wall, simple rim and low ring foot; incised mark on the wall.
Bowl with curving wall and low ring foot; row of impressed circles/ovals on the rim band as decoration.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form AA
description: Flat-based dish imitating African Red Slip Form 61; undecorated versions exist, some with stamped decoration in African Style A.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form BB
description: Shallow bowl or dish copying African Red Slip Form 67, with a low foot and poorly modelled rim; type-specimens plain but stamped decoration likely on some.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form CC
description: Deep bowl with curved wall sloping slightly inward at the rim; low foot; rouletted decoration.
cross_refs: Griffiths LAAA xiv (1927) pl. LIX 16 = LX 15

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form DD
description: Deep bowl with straight steep wall and low foot; rouletted decoration.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form EE
description: Large shallow dish with a heavy upright rim flanged at the bottom and a small low foot; stamped decoration; likely forerunner of Forms H-I.
cross_refs: Armant Type 12B (Bucheum iii pl. CLIV, no. 7)

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form FF
description: Dish with a low sloping wall and a vertical rim that is grooved or flanged; low foot; offset where wall meets floor; a shallow variant of Form J. Larger examples stamped, smaller ones plain.
Carinated bowl with vertical/incurving upper wall and low foot.
Carinated bowl with grooved upper wall and low foot.
Small bowl with curving wall.
Carinated bowl with incised/combed decoration on the upper wall and low foot.
Bowl on a splaying foot with oblique rouletting/hatching on the wall.
Shallow open dish with sloping floor on a low ring foot.
Shallow flaring dish with simple rim.
Shallow flaring dish with thickened rim.
Shallow flaring dish with offset interior.
Large shallow dish with sloping floor and thickened rim.

Dish with shallow sloping floor and thickened rim that is concave or slightly flanged outside, set off from the floor inside by an offset/concave band; low foot. Coarse rouletting and a slight carination usually on the exterior; interior mostly plain.
Bowl/dish with offset wall and low foot.
Dish with thickened/flanged rim and grooved wall on a low foot.
Small deep bowl/cup with a pouring spout or lip.
Deep bowl with flaring wall and thickened rim.
Small bowl with projecting spout/lip.
Deep bowl with curving wall and low foot.
Deep flaring bowl with thickened rim.
Small bowl with projecting spout/lip.
Bowl with flaring wall on a low foot.
Deep bowl with everted/thickened rim.
Deep bowl with thickened rim bearing rouletting near the rim.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form GG
description: Dish with a shallow sloping floor and an upright rim that hooks slightly inward, with grooves at top and bottom; low foot; undecorated. Possibly a variant of forms G or I.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form HH
description: Large plate with a rounded rim slightly rolled on the underside and a high foot; central poorly impressed cross with pendants (stamp Group B, elongated), no other decoration.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form II
description: Plate similar to the preceding but with a heavy knobbed rim; undecorated. High foot.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form JJ
description: Plate similar to preceding forms but with a simple tapering rim; medium-sized or smaller. High foot.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form KK
description: Rather shallow small bowl imitating African RSW forms; short flat rim and high foot; usually a single central stamp encircled by a groove.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form LL
description: Similar to KK but larger, with a short rim; groove around the floor.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form MM
description: Small bowl as KK but with a low upright wall, the rim set off by a groove; stamped cross within a central groove.

id: Egyptian Red Slip Ware Form NN
description: Small bowl with a heavy drooping rim formed by a small bead above and a thick overhanging roll below (almost a separate flange); low foot. Some examples have rouletting on the wall.
Shallow open dish with sloping floor and a crudely shaped rounded foot; a rarer shape, possibly modelled on an African Red Slip prototype.
Dish/shallow bowl with sloping floor and a knobbed rim; floor decorated with two separate grooves or pairs of grooves; rounded crude foot.
Flat-based dish with stamped decoration on the floor; closely imitates a Cypriot Red Slip prototype.
Profile of an open dish/bowl with a flaring curved wall rising to a plain rim; faint grooving on the interior.
Profile of a shallow dish with a curving wall and a thickened/everted rim.
Profile of a bowl with a strongly curved lower wall rising to a simple rim.
Profile of a bowl with a curving wall and rim; rim area shows incised/notched decoration.
Decorative detail: a scalloped/wavy band with rosettes and rouletted lines, plus a separate fan-shaped panel with a heart/leaf motif.
Decorative detail: two grooved lines above rosette/disc stamps flanking a barred motif.
Decorative detail: hatched/oblique band over concentric-circle stamps with a small triangular motif below.
Decorative detail: a row of repeated stamped motifs beneath the rim; below, scroll/spiral and leaf appliqué motifs.
Decorative detail: radiating panels filled with cross-hatching and zig-zag, arranged around stamped roundels.
